## 2026.4.21

### Changes

- OpenAI/images: default the bundled image-generation provider and live media smoke tests to `gpt-image-2`, and advertise the newer 2K/4K OpenAI size hints in image-generation docs and tool metadata.

### Fixes

- Plugins/doctor: repair bundled plugin runtime dependencies from doctor paths so packaged installs can recover missing channel/provider dependencies without broad core dependency installs.
- Image generation: log failed provider/model candidates at warn level before automatic provider fallback, so OpenAI image failures are visible in the gateway log even when a later provider succeeds.
- Auth/commands: require owner identity (an owner-candidate match or internal `operator.admin`) for owner-enforced commands instead of treating wildcard channel `allowFrom` or empty owner-candidate lists as sufficient, so non-owner senders can no longer reach owner-only commands through a permissive fallback when `enforceOwnerForCommands=true` and `commands.ownerAllowFrom` is unset. (#69774) Thanks @drobison00.
- Slack: preserve thread aliases in runtime outbound sends so generic runtime sends stay in the intended Slack thread when the caller supplies `threadTs`. (#62947) Thanks @bek91.
- Browser: reject invalid `ax<N>` accessibility refs in act paths immediately instead of waiting for the browser action timeout. (#69924) Thanks @Patrick-Erichsen.
- npm/install: mirror the `node-domexception` alias into root `package.json` `overrides`, so npm installs stop surfacing the deprecated `google-auth-library -> gaxios -> node-fetch -> fetch-blob -> node-domexception` chain pulled through Pi/Google runtime deps. Thanks @vincentkoc.

key_changes: Auth/commands: 修复所有者命令权限校验漏洞，防止非所有者通过通配符配置绕过权限限制（安全修复）
Plugins/doctor: 修复插件运行时依赖项恢复机制，打包安装现在可以独立修复缺失的 channel/provider 依赖
Image generation: 改进失败日志记录，OpenAI 图像生成失败会在回退前记录 warn 级别日志
Browser: 立即拒绝无效的 ax<N> 可访问性引用，避免等待浏览器操作超时
OpenAI/images: 默认使用 gpt-image-2 模型并支持 2K/4K 高分辨率尺寸
ai_summary.summary_cn: 该版本主要修复了多个安全问题和一个权限漏洞：认证模块修复了所有者命令的身份校验逻辑（安全修复），防止非所有者通过宽松配置绕过权限；插件系统改进了依赖恢复机制，打包安装可独立修复缺失依赖；同时改进了图像生成默认模型为 gpt-image-2 并支持更高分辨率，以及优化了浏览器可访问性验证和图像生成失败日志。

issue_insights.summary_brief: 本期共监测到 5 类跨仓库共性问题，其中"任务执行时抛出通用错误导致主流程阻断"影响最广，覆盖 51 个仓库；其次为"启动崩溃"（依赖缺失、配置不匹配、内网下载失败等）影响 11 仓库，"设置保存导致关联配置丢失"影响 14 仓库。P0 级别问题集中于 session_state 和 startup_crash，建议优先排查会话状态管理与依赖一致性。
global_highlights: 跨仓库 P0 共性问题：保存 LLM 设置时意外重置 MCP 服务器、Tavily 等关联配置，根因为新设置系统的状态回滚逻辑缺陷，影响 14+ 仓库
跨仓库 P0 共性问题：启动阶段崩溃（依赖缺失、配置 schema 不匹配、ACP 运行时初始化失败、内网下载失败），属主流程阻断
跨仓库 P1 共性问题：任务执行时抛出通用 'error' 消息，用户无法定位根因，需统一错误传播链
跨仓库 P2 共性问题：Dashboard 概览页 Token 计数虚高 3 倍（嵌套 span 重复聚合），影响成本追踪与资源规划准确性

source_issues.title: Case mismatch in custom provider model name breaks `context_limit` lookup

signals.topic: Azure PostgreSQL with Entra ID: AsyncEngine dispose attribute is read-only causing server startup crash
signals.summary: Self-hosted Phoenix instances crash immediately on startup when using Azure managed identity (Entra ID) for PostgreSQL authentication. SQLAlchemy's AsyncEngine uses __slots__, making the dispose attribute read-only, which prevents Phoenix from patching it to close the Azure credential. Users are completely blocked from deploying Phoenix in Azure environments.
signals.review_reason: Two independent users reported identical crashes at startup with the same stack trace, confirming a consistent blocking bug for Azure self-hosted deployments. count=2 meets the frequency threshold and the crash is at the critical startup gate — users cannot start the service at all. High confidence due to clear error trace and reproduction in a specific but common deployment scenario (Azure + PostgreSQL + Entra ID).

source_issues.title: [BUG]: AttributeError: 'AsyncEngine' object attribute 'dispose' is read-only when using Azure PostgreSQL with Entra ID

signals.topic: Playground: GraphQL contract mismatch causes runtime validation errors and service outage across provider connections

signals.review_reason: A confirmed production Playground outage with explicit user impact (runtime GraphQL validation errors blocking Playground use) and labeled 'priority: high' by maintainer. While count=1, the severity is high: the feature was completely unavailable and the root cause spans the full stack. The issue documents an actual incident, not a speculative risk. P1 rather than P0 because count=1 and it was an isolated incident rather than a recurring user-reported pattern.

Did you mean 'endpointUrl'?" The issue explicitly documents the incident and proposes systemic fixes to prevent recurrence. Labeled 'priority: high' by maintainer.

While not a workflow blocker, it directly undermines Phoenix's core value proposition of accurate observability and will affect billing and cost planning decisions. count=1 and non-blocking nature make it P2 rather than P1.

signals.topic: TUI event listeners leak memory because they are never cleaned up on session switches
signals.summary: event.on() and event.subscribe() calls in the TUI are never unsubscribed. Each session switch leaves orphaned listeners and closures that GC cannot reclaim, causing progressive memory growth and eventual OOM on long-running instances.
aliases: orphaned TUI listeners on session switch
memory leak from uncleared event subscriptions
signals.review_reason: Memory leak is a confirmed code defect (no cleanup path for TUI event listeners). Progressively degrades stability — long-running instances accumulate unreclaimable memory until OOM. Classified as P1 rather than P0 because the impact requires time/exposure rather than being immediately blocking.

source_issues.title: TUI event listeners leak memory because they're never cleaned up
source_issues.evidence: Explicitly states event listeners are never unsubscribed. Repeated session switches leave orphaned closures unreclaimable by GC. Confirmed in code — no cleanup path exists. Can accumulate to OOM on long-running instances.

signals.topic: Beta streaming accumulator silently drops content blocks due to missing type variants in ParsedBetaContentBlock union
signals.summary: ParsedBetaContentBlock is missing BetaToolSearchToolResultBlock and BetaWebFetchToolResultBlock, causing pydantic discriminated-union resolution to fail and silently drop these blocks from stream.get_final_message().content. Users streaming responses that include tool_search or web_fetch results lose data entirely with no error or warning.
aliases: content blocks silently dropped in streaming
signals.review_reason: Two related issues both about beta streaming accumulator type gaps: #1422 causes silent data loss (tool_search/web_fetch result blocks dropped from get_final_message), #1421 causes missing event notifications for server_tool_use input JSON. Both affect beta streaming users with real data integrity and observability impact. Combined count=2 with concrete code-level root cause.

source_issues.title: ParsedBetaContentBlock union missing tool_search/web_fetch result blocks — stream accumulator drops them from get_final_message()
source_issues.evidence: Code comparison shows BetaContentBlock includes BetaToolSearchToolResultBlock and BetaWebFetchToolResultBlock but ParsedBetaContentBlock omits both. Impact: pydantic discriminated-union resolution fails and blocks are silently coerced or dropped. Users lose data with no error/warning.

source_issues.title: BetaInputJsonEvent not fired for server_tool_use blocks during streaming

Users must manually subscribe to BetaRawContentBlockDeltaEvent with BetaInputJSONDelta delta.

signals.topic: Batch API intermittent 404 NotFoundError crashes application on batches.results() and batches.create()
signals.summary: Batch API operations (create, retrieve, results) intermittently return 404 NotFoundError due to server-side propagation delay, crashing the application at critical points (especially batches.results() which internally calls retrieve). All operations eventually succeed on retry, but the initial failure is unhandled and blocks production workloads.
signals.review_reason: Application crashes (NotFoundError) at the critical batches.results() call with a full traceback. Three distinct failure modes documented in production within a 15-minute window. The crash is unhandled by default, requiring users to manually catch NotFoundError and implement fallback logic. This blocks the primary batch result retrieval workflow.

source_issues.title: Intermittent `NotFoundError (404)` on Batch API
source_issues.evidence: Issue provides full traceback showing batches.results() crashes with NotFoundError (404). Three distinct failure cases documented within a 15-minute window: (1) retrieve() returns 404 within 1 second of creation, (2) results() crashes with traceback after status was confirmed ended, (3) create() returns 404. Workaround requires catching NotFoundError and falling back to messages.create(), demonstrating real production impact.

signals.topic: Streaming aggregator does not propagate message_delta.container field, breaking code_execution continuation
signals.summary: When using messages.stream() with code_execution_20260120, stream.get_final_message().container is None because the streaming accumulator never merges delta.container from message_delta SSE events. This causes a BadRequestError 400 on the second turn of any multi-turn tool-use loop with streaming, since container_id is required. Users must manually subscribe to RawMessageDeltaEvent to extract the container id, or fall back to non-streaming mode.
signals.review_reason: Breaks the core streaming workflow for code_execution_20260120 tool. The BadRequestError 400 on the second API turn is a hard failure that blocks multi-turn tool-use loops in streaming mode. Reproduction is end-to-end with full traceback. The only workaround (manual SSE event parsing) is non-obvious and represents a significant DX regression vs non-streaming behavior.

source_issues.title: `get_final_message()` does not propagate `message_delta.container` into aggregated Message (breaks code_execution continuation)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction code provided showing streaming final.container=None vs non-streaming correctly populated. Full traceback for the resulting BadRequestError (400) on the second API call: 'container_id is required when there are pending tool uses generated by code execution with tools'. Root cause identified in src/anthropic/lib/streaming/_messages.py accumulate_event() — delta.container is never merged. No workaround via SDK happy-path API; manual SSE event interception required.

signals.topic: Managed Agents MCP client only supports SSE transport — incompatible with servers using Streamable HTTP
signals.summary: Managed Agents (client.beta.agents, client.beta.sessions) only supports SSE transport for MCP servers, but servers like Apify deprecated SSE on April 1, 2026 and now exclusively support Streamable HTTP. This completely breaks Managed Agents with affected MCP servers at initialization with 'SSE data line is not valid JSON'. No workaround available — the entire feature is unusable with any Streamable HTTP-only MCP server.
signals.review_reason: Managed Agents feature is completely unusable with Streamable HTTP-only MCP servers (major provider Apify dropped SSE April 1, 2026). The error occurs at session initialization, blocking the entire feature. The review_reason notes the implementation already exists in Claude Code but is absent from the SDK's Managed Agents layer, making this a clear gap rather than a missing feature. Single repo but clear user impact with temporal urgency (Apify SSE shutdown is a recent breaking change).

source_issues.title: Managed Agents MCP client only supports SSE transport — incompatible with servers that have dropped SSE (e.g. Apify)
source_issues.evidence: Apify deprecated SSE endpoint April 1, 2026. Full error: "MCP server 'apify' initialize failed: SSE data line is not valid JSON" — 405 Method Not Allowed. Agent falls back to other tools and never uses Apify. Explicitly stated: no workaround available on client side. Note that Claude Code itself already supports Streamable HTTP MCP (via claude mcp add --transport http), proving the implementation exists but isn't wired into Managed Agents.

signals.topic: Streaming overloaded error crashes LangChain integration without clear handling guidance
signals.summary: When using the SDK via LangChain's ChatAnthropic in streaming mode, an intermittent 'Overloaded' error from the API causes APIStatusError to be raised mid-stream, crashing the LangChain chain. The error occurs approximately 1 in 100 requests in production. Users lack clear guidance on how to handle retry for streaming scenarios where partial tokens have already been yielded.
signals.review_reason: Intermittent API overloaded errors crash streaming pipelines mid-stream with no documented retry pattern for streaming context. While the error originates from the API server rather than the SDK, the SDK is the layer where retry logic and error handling guidance should be documented. The 1-in-100 failure rate in production is non-trivial. Marked P2 (not P0/P1) because it is a third-party integration (LangChain) and the root cause is server-side load rather than SDK bug, but it still represents a real production pain point.

source_issues.title: How to handle Anthropic 'Overloaded' error when streaming in langchain
source_issues.evidence: Full traceback showing APIStatusError with overloaded_error thrown mid-stream in a LangChain RAG application. Error occurs ~1 in 100 requests in production. The streaming context makes retry non-trivial since partial tokens have been yielded. Issue explicitly asks for guidance on handling retries — no documented pattern exists. Labels include 'documentation'.

signals.topic: Invalid tool_use.id format (functions.{ToolName}:{N}) causes API 400 error on session resume, blocking session resumption entirely
signals.summary: The SDK generates tool_use.id values containing dots and colons (e.g., 'functions.AskUserQuestion:1') which violate the API's ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ pattern. During session resume, these invalid IDs are replayed verbatim, causing a 400 API error that makes session resume completely non-functional.
aliases: session resume 400 error due to invalid tool_use.id
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：session resume完全不可用，API 400错误。工具ID格式违规是根本原因，用户无法在断点后恢复会话。证据充分：issue包含完整的API错误响应、非法ID样例（functions.AskUserQuestion:1）和合法ID对比。

source_issues.title: Invalid tool_use.id format during session resume causes API 400 error
source_issues.evidence: API returns: messages.7.content.1.tool_use.id: String should match pattern '^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$' with IDs 'functions.AskUserQuestion:1' containing illegal '.' and ':' characters

signals.topic: ProcessError exit_code/stderr stripped during error propagation; users see generic Exception with hard-coded 'Check stderr output for details' placeholder
signals.summary: When the CLI subprocess exits non-zero, the original ProcessError (with structured exit_code and stderr fields) is destroyed through three compounding defects: stderr is never captured (hard-coded literal), the exception type is reduced to str() in the message reader, and it is re-raised as a bare Exception. Users cannot catch ProcessError, cannot access exit_code, and stderr is always the literal placeholder string — making command failure diagnosis impossible without forking the SDK.
aliases: ProcessError type destroyed in error propagation
generic Exception instead of ProcessError on CLI failure
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：错误处理链完全失效。ProcessError被降级为str，exit_code和stderr全部丢失，用户在并发/CI场景下无法对CLI失败进行任何有意义的诊断。issue提供了完整的三重缺陷定位（subprocess_cli.py、query.py两处），证据为可运行的reproduction script。

source_issues.title: ProcessError exit_code/stderr stripped during error propagation; users see generic Exception with hard-coded 'Check stderr output for details' placeholder
source_issues.evidence: Verified reproduction shows: caught type is 'Exception' (not ProcessError), .exit_code and .stderr attributes are absent. Original stderr is a hard-coded literal never capturing real subprocess output. Closed issues #515, #282, #238 all hit variants of this.

signals.topic: bwrap sandbox does not mount /etc/hosts; breaks localhost DNS resolution in Docker containers, blocking all AWS service calls
signals.summary: The bwrap sandbox creates an isolated filesystem/network namespace but does not bind-mount /etc/hosts from the host. Without /etc/hosts, there is no mapping from localhost to 127.0.0.1, so any process inside the sandbox that needs to resolve localhost fails. In Docker containers where outbound traffic is routed through a proxy at localhost:3128 (standard in AWS Bedrock AgentCore runtimes), all AWS service calls via boto3 fail with DNS resolution errors. Users are forced to disable the sandbox entirely (sandbox.enabled=false) to restore pre-2.1.92 behavior.
aliases: bwrap sandbox DNS resolution failure in containers
localhost resolution broken in sandboxed Docker environment
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：在容器化/AWS Bedrock场景下，所有AWS服务调用（boto3）全部失败。用户被迫禁用sandbox来绕过，严重影响安全隔离能力。回归问题（2.1.81→2.1.92引入），证据包含完整错误栈和reproduction步骤。

source_issues.title: bwrap sandbox does not mount /etc/hosts — breaks localhost DNS resolution in containers
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible error: socket.gaierror: [Errno -3] Temporary failure in name resolution; urllib3.exceptions.ProxyError with NameResolutionError on 'localhost'; botocore.exceptions.ProxyConnectionError. Regression: worked in CLI 2.1.81, broke in 2.1.92. Workaround is to disable sandbox entirely, sacrificing security.

signals.topic: Prompt cache TTL not exposed via SDK; no extended-cache-ttl-2025-04-11 beta support, capping cross-session cost amortization
signals.summary: The SDK does not expose cache TTL controls for the system prompt prefix. The SdkBeta type only includes 'context-1m-2025-08-07' and cannot pass 'extended-cache-ttl-2025-04-11'. ClaudeAgentOptions has no cache_ttl or cache_control field. The bundled CLI doesn't expose a TTL flag. For workloads running thousands of short-lived sessions per day against a shared system prompt (15-20K tokens), the default 5-minute TTL caps cross-session amortization, whereas a 1h TTL would significantly improve cache hit rates and reduce cost. One org reports ~$11K/14 days of Sonnet agentic spend affected.
aliases: system prompt cache TTL too short for production workloads
signals.review_reason: 明显成本损失：默认5分钟TTL导致跨会话缓存命中率低，实际增加token消耗。用户报告单客户$11K/14天受影响。功能缺失（extended-cache-ttl beta不支持）阻止了成本优化，属于关键功能不可用（cache TTL control）。

source_issues.title: Expose prompt-cache `cache_control` / 1h TTL on `ClaudeAgentOptions.system_prompt` (Bedrock + Messages API)
source_issues.evidence: Cost evidence: ~$11K/14 days of Sonnet agentic spend affected. SdkBeta only has 'context-1m-2025-08-07'. No cache_ttl field in ClaudeAgentOptions. Workload is 1000s of short multi-turn sessions per day with burst cadence — classic 1h TTL territory.

signals.topic: setting_sources=[] does not filter OAuth-fetched MCP servers; causes test harness contamination and noisy stderr in isolated environments
signals.summary: ClaudeAgentOptions(setting_sources=[]) is intended to isolate test harnesses from ambient operator environment (user/project/local settings, agents, skills, plugins). However, it does not filter claude.ai-account MCP servers fetched via OAuth (Figma, Gmail, Calendar, Drive). Isolated test harnesses using setting_sources=[] still pull in operator's account MCPs, causing noisy stderr debug lines ([claudeai-mcp] Fetching...), diagnostic contamination between test runs, and slower initialization. A workaround exists via extra_args={'strict-mcp-config': None} but it is undocumented.
aliases: OAuth MCP servers not blocked by setting_sources=[]
test harness polluted by account MCPs despite isolation settings
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：测试环境被account MCP污染，stderr充满噪音行，测试结果不确定。setting_sources=[]的语义承诺与实际不符，用户需要undocumented workaround才能隔离。虽非阻断但严重影响自动化测试可信度。

source_issues.title: setting_sources=[] does not filter OAuth-fetched claude.ai-account MCP servers
source_issues.evidence: Even with mcp_servers={} and setting_sources=[], stderr shows '[claudeai-mcp] Fetching...' and MCPs are connected. Workaround via 'strict-mcp-config' extra_args exists but is undocumented. Workaround landed in production at https://github.com/brandonrdug/projectmeta/pull/100.

signals.topic: beta.sessions stream starvation — 4/5 parallel and serial streams fail with TypeError before any events arrive
signals.summary: When firing multiple beta.sessions.events.stream() calls, 4 of 5 consistently fail with TypeError: stream error terminated before any events arrive. Even serialized (1 session at a time), 4 of 5 still fail. The standard Messages API works reliably with identical auth/prompt/model, isolating the issue to beta.sessions lifecycle.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断: beta.sessions stream 是 SDK 的核心会话 API，80%% 失败率直接导致会话无法建立。用户被迫回退到标准 Messages API，失去了 sessions 特有的状态管理能力。错误在串行场景下依然发生，排除并发因素，表明是底层会话生命周期的结构性缺陷。

source_issues.title: beta.sessions stream starvation — 4 of 5 parallel (and serial) sessions fail with TypeError: stream error: terminated before any events
source_issues.evidence: 80% failure rate (4/5) across parallel and serial attempts; sawAnyEvent=false for all failures; stream never produced a single chunk; workaround required rewrites to client.messages.create

signals.topic: Hardcoded 60s HTTP timeout on MCP POST requests is not configurable
signals.summary: A recent release added a hardcoded 60-second timeout value for MCP POST requests that cannot be configured by users. Operations longer than 60s fail with 'The operation timed out'.
signals.review_reason: 工作流阻断: MCP 服务器是 SDK 工具生态的核心扩展机制，硬编码 60s 超时导致长时间运行的任务（如大数据查询、复杂构建）无法完成。用户没有任何配置手段绕过此限制，核心工作流被迫中断。

source_issues.title: Hardcoded 60s HTTP timeout on MCP POST requests does not seem to be configurable
source_issues.evidence: Users cannot configure the 60s MCP POST timeout; operations exceeding 60s fail with 'The operation timed out'; hardcoded constant found in bundled cli.js binary

signals.topic: Background task_notification events buffered until next send() — real-time notifications delayed or collapsed into wrong model context
signals.summary: When a background Bash command completes while the application is idle (not actively in a for await loop), the task_notification is buffered in the SDK and only delivered when the next send() call triggers a drain. The model sees the notification and the new user message as back-to-back user turns, responding to both together.
signals.review_reason: 实时性破坏 + 模型上下文错误: 后台任务完成通知被延迟到下一条用户消息才送达，导致模型同时看到通知和新用户消息并一起响应。这破坏了实时反馈的语义，使模型行为不可预测。对于依赖后台任务完成通知驱动下一步操作的应用，这是严重的时序缺陷。

source_issues.title: Background task_notification events are lazy-drained: buffered until next send()
source_issues.evidence: task_notification events are buffered during idle periods and only delivered on next send(), causing the model to respond to both the notification and new user message together; no public API to peek at pending messages

signals.topic: IPv6 happy-eyeballs fallback failure in bundled cli.js — Vertex AI OAuth hangs on Tailscale/dual-stack networks
signals.summary: The bundled cli.js uses undici as its HTTP client. On networks where Tailscale provides an IPv6 ULA address and IPv6 is not routable to Google, undici's autoSelectFamily fails to fall back to IPv4, causing OAuth token refresh to hang silently. This blocks all chat messages on Vertex AI backend entirely.
signals.review_reason: 认证阻断: 在有 Tailscale 的双栈网络环境中，OAuth 令牌刷新无限挂起，导致所有聊天消息完全失败。这是一个影响特定网络配置用户的关键功能不可用问题，且 Node 原生 https 模块能正确处理，证明了 SDK 捆绑的 undici 客户端存在缺陷。

source_issues.title: Bundled cli.js fails IPv6 happy-eyeballs fallback — Vertex AI OAuth hangs on dual-stack networks
source_issues.evidence: OAuth token refresh to Google hangs indefinitely on dual-stack networks with Tailscale; undici autoSelectFamily fails to fall back to IPv4; all chat messages fail with empty error reason; Node native https module handles this correctly

signals.topic: Stop hook callback never invoked when only JS callback is registered (no shell-command hook paired)
signals.summary: When registering a Stop hook as a pure JavaScript callback via hooks.Stop, with no corresponding shell-command hook for the same event, the callback is never invoked on end_turn. This is distinct from PostToolUse fast-path (#280) where the callback fires but return value is discarded — here the callback never fires at all.
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降: Stop hook 是用户控制 agent 行为的核心扩展点，文档明确说明 Stop hooks fire on every turn completion。当回调完全不被调用时，用户无法通过 hook 拦截或干预 turn 结束流程，强制要求重做或注入自定义逻辑的用例完全失效。

source_issues.title: Stop hook callback never invoked in v0.2.117 when only JS callback is registered
source_issues.evidence: Stop hook JS callback never fires across 5+ independent end_turn cycles; observed in production; callback registration shape matches types; workaround requires app-level loop inspection, bypassing the hook abstraction entirely

signals.topic: GitHub Actions cache save fails with 5-retry HTML error pattern on successive PR runs (key+ref collision)
signals.summary: On pull_request synchronize events, the post-job cache save consistently fails with 5 exponential-backoff retries, each burning 20-30 seconds. The GitHub cache API returns a permanent "key already exists" HTML error that @actions/cache misinterprets as a transient failure. Users lose 20-30 seconds per additional commit on every PR.
signals.review_reason: Real user workflow pain: every additional commit on a PR wastes 20-30 seconds due to 5 unnecessary retries of a permanent conflict error. Quantified time loss per run. Affects the default pull_request trigger pattern used by most users.

source_issues.title: Cache save fails with 5-retry HTML-error pattern on successive runs against the same PR ref (key+ref collision)
source_issues.evidence: Bug report includes full reproduction steps showing tar compression completing (35MB at 58MB/s) then 5 retry attempts each burning 3000ms+ backoff. Labels: bug, performance. User impact quantified: ~20-30 seconds per failure per additional commit on every PR.

signals.topic: Agent mode leaves session summary comment stale with 'Running...' status after agent finishes
signals.summary: In agent mode, the session summary comment (created by the SDK before the action's main function receives control) has an undefined commentId at cleanup time. The post-job cleanup skips the updateCommentLink call, leaving the GitHub PR comment permanently showing 'Running...' even after the agent has finished. Users see misleading status and cannot rely on the comment for results.
signals.review_reason: Agent mode is a key feature. Stale 'Running...' comment misleads collaborators reviewing the PR. Clear root cause identified. P2 because it is cosmetic/UX rather than blocking the agent's core functionality, but still a real user experience problem.

source_issues.title: Agent mode discards session summary: cleanup phase gates updateCommentLink on commentId, agent mode hard-codes commentId: undefined
source_issues.evidence: Bug report explains root cause: session summary comment is created by SDK before action main() runs, so commentId is undefined in cleanup phase. updateCommentLink is skipped. Result: comment stays 'Running...' permanently. Labels: bug, feature-request.

signals.topic: Bundled MCP servers silently fail to spawn on pull_request events with no error or warning shown
signals.summary: When the action runs on a pull_request event, bundled MCP servers fail to spawn silently. The mcp_servers array ends up empty even though the config was built correctly. No error or warning is shown to the user, so they do not know why their MCP tools are unavailable. This breaks a key functionality users depend on, with zero visibility into the failure.
signals.review_reason: Silent failure of a key feature (MCP servers) is a significant user pain: users configure MCP servers expecting them to work, they silently do not, and there is no error message to indicate the problem. The failure is reproducible (pull_request trigger). P1 because it blocks a core feature with no user-visible error.

source_issues.title: Bundled MCP servers silently fail to spawn on pull_request events (mcp_servers empty despite correct config build)
source_issues.evidence: Bug labeled 'mcp' and 'p2'. Key functionality (MCP servers) fails silently with zero error output. User has no indication of failure or its cause. Labels: bug, mcp.

signals.topic: claude-sonnet-4-6 produces repeated empty turns with stop_reason: null, causing agent to loop indefinitely
signals.summary: claude-sonnet-4-6 (the default model in many cases) produces empty turns with stop_reason: null and output_tokens: 8, repeating this behavior instead of properly concluding. This causes the agent to get stuck in an infinite loop or produce no useful output. Reproduces on both v1.0.100 and v1.0.101, indicating a regression or model compatibility issue.
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure: the agent's primary task (completing a meaningful response) is broken. Empty turns with null stop_reason cause the agent to loop or stall. Affects the default Sonnet model. Reproduces across two consecutive releases confirming it is not an isolated incident.

source_issues.title: claude-sonnet-4-6 silent-fails with repeated empty turns (stop_reason: null, output_tokens: 8) — reproduces on v1.0.100 and v1.0.101
source_issues.evidence: Bug labeled 'bug', 'provider:1p'. Reproduces on two consecutive action versions. Behavior: stop_reason null, output_tokens 8 (essentially empty). This is a main-flow failure that prevents the agent from completing its task. Labels confirm it as a bug.

signals.topic: Action breaks completely in air-gapped/network-isolated environments where claude.ai is unreachable
signals.summary: In environments where claude.ai is unreachable (air-gapped, VPN-only, restricted networks), v1.0.100 install.sh fails silently and the SDK bundled binary is bypassed, breaking the action entirely. Users in these environments cannot use the action despite having a valid setup.
signals.review_reason: Action completely non-functional in air-gapped/isolated network environments. Silent failure of install.sh with no error message. This is a significant blocker for enterprise users with restricted network access. P1 due to complete workflow failure.

source_issues.title: v1.0.100 breaks environments where claude.ai is unreachable (install.sh silently fails, SDK bundled binary bypassed)
source_issues.evidence: Bug labeled 'bug'. install.sh silently fails and SDK bundled binary is bypassed. Affects users in air-gapped/restricted network environments. The action is completely broken in these environments. Labels: bug.

signals.topic: Claude Sonnet regression: model ignores context, skips investigation, bypasses claude.md rules
signals.summary: Claude Sonnet 4.7 performs shallow context analysis, ignores claude.md rules, skips detailed investigation before proposing solutions — a significant regression from 4.6. Also causes loss of session-to-session continuity.
signals.review_reason: Model regression affecting core workflow quality. Sonnet 4.7 ignoring context and rules means users must invest significant extra effort to guide the model correctly — a clear cost/efficiency loss. Count=2 with duplicate link confirmed. Downgraded from P0 because main flow is not technically blocked, but the productivity degradation is substantial.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Claude 3.5 Sonnet regression: Insufficient context analysis before proposing solutions
source_issues.evidence: User reports: 'Opus 4.7 is making more and more logical errors… it skips over detail and proposes interventions in the wrong places… this is a SIGNIFICANT REGRESSION from 4.6… I DO NOT TRUST 4.7.' Also: 'it's like it's ignoring rules and claude.md completely.' Multiple affected areas: context analysis, instruction following, session continuity.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Not Malware over and over
source_issues.evidence: User reports: 'Claude thinks everything is malware. Every session, anywhere.' First-message occurrence. Duplicate label applied, confirming a known cluster of false-positive malware detection.

signals.topic: Claude Cowork UI unusable due to JSON parse errors
signals.summary: Users constantly encounter 'JSON Parse error: Unable to parse JSON string' errors in the Cowork desktop application, making the feature completely unusable from one day to the next.
signals.review_reason: Cowork is a core product feature (desktop collaboration UI). JSON parse errors make the entire Cowork experience unusable — a primary workflow is blocked. Regression confirmed by user. High severity despite count=1 because the feature is completely broken for affected users.

source_issues.title: [BUG] JSON errors in Claude Cowork
source_issues.evidence: User reports: 'I am constantly getting JSON errors in the cowork desktop UI, it's unusable for me right now.' Error message: 'API Error: JSON Parse error: Unable to parse JSON string.' Regression — worked in a previous version.

signals.topic: Claude-in-Chrome extension fails to connect to Claude Code CLI despite matching accounts
signals.summary: The Claude-in-Chrome browser extension shows 'installed and enabled' but cannot connect to the Claude Code CLI. The MCP handshake never completes even when accounts match and MCP server reports successful reconnection.
signals.review_reason: The Claude-in-Chrome extension is a key integration feature. When the handshake fails silently, users lose browser automation capabilities — a key differentiating feature of Claude Code. The error is deterministic and reproducible with clear steps.

source_issues.title: Claude-in-Chrome extension not connecting to Claude Code (accounts match, handshake never completes)
source_issues.evidence: User reports: '/mcp reconnect on the Claude Code side completes successfully, but the browser handshake never follows.' Error: 'Browser extension is not connected.' Extension works for claude.ai web but not CLI. Account matching confirmed. Critical MCP integration feature blocked.

signals.topic: Account authentication switches incorrectly after re-login, applying wrong API rate limits
signals.summary: After logging out of personal account and re-logging into team account, Claude Code still applies personal account API rate limits instead of team limits. Users are blocked from using team resources.
aliases: Team account limits not applied after logout/login
signals.review_reason: Authentication bug directly causes incorrect API quota enforcement. Users on team accounts are effectively blocked from accessing their correct quota tier. This is a cost/billing issue — users may hit unexpected rate limits or lose access to team resources. Count=1 but high impact warrants P1.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Team vs Pro account API limits incorrectly applied after re-authentication
source_issues.evidence: User reports: 'I logged out from my personal account's Claude Code app, I logged out from claude CLI started via ccs and re-logged in back (team account), but the limit from my personal account is used. This is not acceptable!' Multiple certificate errors also visible in logs. Clear billing/quota impact.

signals.topic: Sub-agents spawned with escalated permission mode bypass user-configured allow/deny rules
signals.summary: The Agent tool allows spawning sub-agents with mode='auto' even when the parent session is in 'default' permission mode. This bypasses user-configured allow/deny/ask rules for the entire sub-agent lifetime (293 tool calls without user approval observed).
aliases: Sub-agent auto mode bypasses permission rules
Agent tool permission escalation security issue
signals.review_reason: Security boundary violation: sub-agents with auto mode run hundreds of tool calls without any user oversight, bypassing the user's explicit allow/deny/ask rules. This is not just a UX issue but a trust model violation. Users in default mode explicitly rely on interactive approval as a security control.

source_issues.title: Sub-agents can escalate permission mode beyond parent session (default → auto)
source_issues.evidence: User reports: 'Agent tool call included mode:auto in its input parameters. Sub-agent executed 293 tool calls over ~34 minutes without user approval.' Session logs provided showing permissionMode:default parent and mode:auto sub-agent. User-configured hooks fired but permission checks bypassed. Clear security/permission model violation.

signals.topic: Skills cookbook prerequisite missing: users unable to follow instructions without knowing to clone GitHub repo
signals.summary: The 'intro to skills' cookbook tells users to 'cd /path/to/claude-cookbooks/skills' but never mentions that they must first clone the GitHub repository. This blocks users from completing the getting-started tutorial.
aliases: missing git clone prerequisite in skills notebook
signals.review_reason: Users are blocked from completing the skills getting-started tutorial because the prerequisites section never mentions cloning the GitHub repo. This is a workflow-blocking documentation gap with a clear reproduction path and direct user frustration testimony.

source_issues.title: [BUG] intro to skills should point at github repo as install prereq
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly describes the blocking experience: 'try to follow the instructions without first having cloned a github repo which is never mentioned, be frustrated'. The prerequisites section omits the git clone step, causing users to hit a dead end immediately.

signals.topic: Managed agents webhook registration not visible in Claude Platform Console — users cannot implement async production patterns
signals.summary: The managed agents cookbook documents a webhook registration feature (under Console Settings → Webhooks) that users cannot find in the actual Platform Console UI. This blocks users from implementing the async production agent loop pattern described in the cookbook.
aliases: webhook settings not found in Console
managed agents async pattern blocked by missing Console UI
signals.review_reason: The cookbook documents webhook registration as a production pattern, but the feature is not discoverable in the Console UI. This blocks users from implementing async agent loops in production — a key use case described in the cookbook itself. The issue is raised as a question but the evidence shows a concrete feature gap causing user confusion.

source_issues.title: [QUESTION] Managed agents webhooks
source_issues.evidence: User reports: 'I found no reference to webhook in the Claude Platform Console. Am I missing something?' — The cookbook explicitly promises a webhook registration path under Console Settings, but the feature is not accessible in the UI, blocking the async production pattern the cookbook describes.

signals.topic: style-configure: always overwrites existing brand files instead of augmenting — no per-file granularity, ignores PROTECTED header, and defaults are not marked for review
signals.summary: style-configure has no augment mode: it either overwrites everything or does nothing. This destroys months of hand-crafted brand documentation when re-running the wizard. The overwrite prompt is binary (no per-file granularity). Files with PROTECTED: header are overwritten despite explicit user intent. Defaulted values are written silently with no review indication.
signals.review_reason: User pain point — 4 related issues all concerning the same core problem: style-configure cannot safely handle existing brand documentation. Combined, these bugs cause irreversible data loss (overwritten v6.0 docs), silent defaulting of important config (voice ID, easing curves), and inability to protect intentionally locked files. count=4 with distinct root causes per issue.

source_issues.title: style-configure: no augment mode — always full overwrite, even on rich existing files
source_issues.evidence: Step-by-step reproduction: (1) run /style-configure on fresh project → generates all 7 files, (2) manually evolve knowledge/brand/style.md over months to v6.0, (3) system introduces new required yaml blocks, (4) re-run /style-configure → all custom content in step 2 is overwritten. Only option is manual editing, defeating the purpose of the wizard.

source_issues.title: style-configure: PROTECTED header in brand files is not respected
source_issues.evidence: Brand files can carry a 'PROTECTED: This file is NEVER synced from core' header. style-configure Phase 5 checks for non-default files and warns, but still overwrites if the user confirms — it does not distinguish protected files. Projects that intentionally protect brand files from automated sync can have those files overwritten.

source_issues.title: style-configure: overwrite prompt is binary — no per-file granularity
source_issues.evidence: Phase 5 presents a single binary 'overwrite all? [y/n]' prompt. Projects with mixed-age brand files (some fresh, some mature v6.0) cannot safely use the wizard without risking overwriting valuable content. No way to selectively overwrite only outdated files.

source_issues.title: style-configure: no yaml block insertion spec for files with existing structure
source_issues.evidence: skill spec defines what yaml blocks to write but not where to insert them in pre-existing rich files. Without insertion anchors, augment logic cannot place blocks without risking misplacement or duplication. Example: style.md with 10 custom sections — the required yaml:brand-config block has no defined insertion point.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: inbound notifications generated by MCP server are not received or displayed by Claude Code — core receive functionality completely broken
signals.summary: The MCP server correctly generates valid JSON-RPC notifications (verified via manual bun server.ts execution — stdout shows correct notifications), but Claude Code 2.1.117 does not process or display them. Terminal dock icon bounces suggesting activity, but no `<channel source="telegram">` tag appears in the session. This is a regression: the plugin's core inbound messaging feature is entirely non-functional.
signals.review_reason: User pain point — core inbound receive functionality is completely broken in the Telegram plugin (outbound works fine). MCP server generates correct notifications but Claude Code silently drops them. Two independent reports with identical symptoms. Users cannot receive Telegram messages at all through the plugin.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin 0.0.6: inbound notifications not received by Claude Code
source_issues.evidence: Outbound reply tool works correctly. MCP server confirmed connected (✔ in /mcp). Bot polls correctly. Manual execution of bun server.ts shows valid JSON-RPC notifications on stdout. signals.topic: ralph-loop: stdin handler shell word-splitting corrupts multi-word flags including --completion-promise, causing premature loop exit
signals.summary: The `--stdin` handler in setup-ralph-loop.sh uses unquoted `set -- \$_RALPH_STDIN_LINE` which performs shell word-splitting on whitespace and ignores quoting. Multi-word `--completion-promise` values are silently truncated to the first token (e.g. `'there were not any improvement'` becomes `'there`), making the stop condition trivially trip and causing premature loop exit with no user indication that the promise was mangled.
signals.review_reason: User pain point — completion-promise is the only way to stop a ralph-loop (besides --max-iterations). When silently corrupted, the loop exits prematurely without user awareness. Clear reproduction + byte-exact root cause analysis provided.

source_issues.title: ralph-loop: --stdin handler word-splits multi-word flag values (silent corruption of --completion-promise)
source_issues.evidence: Multi-word --completion-promise 'there were not any improvement or repair findings' is silently stored as completion_promise: "'there" in the state file. The loop then exits the moment Claude emits that fragment, far sooner than intended, with no indication to the user that the promise was mangled. Verified with concrete reproduction steps.

signals.topic: ralph-loop: cross-session state leak when CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is unset at setup — unrelated sessions get blocked and iteration counters are poisoned
signals.summary: setup-ralph-loop.sh persists `session_id: ${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:-}` which may be empty when the env var is absent. The stop hook guard short-circuits on empty string, causing every session in the project cwd to match and be blocked with the loop prompt. Iteration counters are advanced by whichever session stops first.
signals.review_reason: User pain point — active ralph-loop blocks ALL sessions in the project directory (not just the owning session) and corrupts iteration counters. Verified with a deterministic single-session hook-level reproduction (no two-session setup required). Two independent contributors converged on the same diagnosis.

source_issues.title: ralph-loop: cross-session state leak when CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is unset at setup
source_issues.evidence: Two independent contributors diagnosed the same issue and submitted PRs (#1527, #1529). Concrete reproduction: seeding the state file with empty session_id causes stop-hook to emit block decisions for ALL sessions in the same project directory, not just the owning session. Iteration counters are poisoned by unrelated sessions.

signals.topic: ralph-loop: concurrent loops in same project directory overwrite each other's state file due to hardcoded path — second loop silently breaks the first

signals.review_reason: User pain point — second concurrent ralph-loop silently overwrites and breaks the first. No workaround available. Users running multiple tasks in the same project are blocked.

Users following the docs get compilation errors or runtime failures.
signals.review_reason: While count=1, this is a single issue that aggregates 6 distinct bug categories across 3 languages (Python, Node, TypeScript) affecting a core skill. The evidence clearly shows compilation failures (missing imports, wrong signatures) and runtime failures (wrong attribute names, fabricated API params). This is a textbook case of documentation drift from SDK changes causing user-blocking failures when following the skill.

source_issues.title: Bugs and stale API references in the mcp-builder skill
source_issues.evidence: Issue details 6 distinct categories of wrong/outdated code examples: (1) Pydantic max_items deprecated in v2 → causes warnings/future breakage; (2) ctx.elicit() signature fabricated (no prompt=/input_type params) → runtime failure; (3) lifespan pattern uses wrong attribute names (lifespan_state instead of lifespan_context) → runtime failure; (4) missing Node imports (StreamableHTTPServerTransport, express) → compilation failure; (5) registerResource signature wrong (name-first vs uri-first) and registerResourceList doesn't exist → compilation failure; (6) deprecated raw notification() API used instead of typed helpers → inconsistency with skill's own directive. User DamienOR-dot has a working patched copy and identified all issues by reviewing the docs.

signals.topic: pack.py on macOS bundles .DS_Store into Office archives, causing Microsoft Office to reject/corrupt files
signals.summary: scripts/office/pack.py lacks a filter for .DS_Store files. On macOS, Finder-created .DS_Store entries are bundled into zip archives, and Microsoft Office (per ECMA-376 spec) rejects undeclared archive entries, showing 'found a problem with content' repair dialog or failing to open entirely. LibreOffice is lenient, so CI doesn't catch it.
signals.review_reason: Clear user-blocking workflow failure: macOS users cannot produce valid Office files through pack.py. Verified reproduction with Microsoft 365 for Mac, affecting PPTX/DOCX/XLSX skills (three separate skills share the same pack.py script per SHA db29ed8b). The file either fails to open or triggers a repair dialog — both are data-integrity failures. CI doesn't catch it because LibreOffice is lenient. This meets P0: single repo but the issue is cross-skill (pptx+docx+xlsx), has verified user impact, and directly blocks a primary workflow.

source_issues.title: `pack.py` bundles `.DS_Store` on macOS, causing Office to flag files as corrupt
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction steps provided by user TerryChengTW: (1) unpack PPTX with unpack.py, (2) open folder in Finder (creates .DS_Store), (3) repack with pack.py, (4) open in PowerPoint → repair dialog. Verified on Microsoft 365 for Mac. When .DS_Store deleted before repacking, pack.py produces clean file. Root cause: no filter in the for-loop that zips directory contents. Impact is document corruption/non-opening, which is a clear data-loss risk for user-generated Office files.

signals.topic: docx skill TableOfContents renders empty in Google Docs due to missing cachedEntries option
signals.summary: The docx skill's TableOfContents example creates .docx files that display correctly in Word but render as empty placeholders in Google Docs. Clicking 'refresh' produces entries whose hyperlinks don't resolve. Root cause: docx-js only emits populated TOC cache when cachedEntries is provided; Google Docs relies on the cache since it doesn't run field updates on open.
signals.review_reason: Table of Contents is a fundamental document feature. When users generate .docx files with the skill and open them in Google Docs (a very common workflow), the TOC is empty and hyperlinks don't resolve. This is a visible feature regression — the document appears broken even though it works in Word. Clear user impact for the common Google Docs integration path.

source_issues.title: [Bug] docx skill: TableOfContents renders empty in Google Docs without cachedEntries
source_issues.evidence: User muscal identified root cause: docx-js only emits populated <w:sdt> cache when cachedEntries is provided. Google Docs does not run TOC field update on open and relies on cached content. Symptom: TOC renders empty, refresh produces entries with non-resolving hyperlinks. .docx works fine in Word. Clear cross-platform compatibility failure for a core document feature.

signals.topic: Case-sensitive model name comparison silently causes wrong context_limit for custom providers — falls back to 128K default
signals.summary: When a custom provider model name contains uppercase letters (e.g. 'GLM-5.1', 'Qwen3-Coder-480B'), goose performs a strict case-sensitive lookup of the context_limit, which fails because config.yaml stores the model name in lowercase. The failure is silent — users get the default 128K context limit with no indication that the configured limit was ignored.
aliases: model name case sensitivity silent failure
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss: custom provider models with uppercase names (a common naming pattern) always get the wrong context_limit with no user-visible indication. This directly causes context truncation for affected models without any error or warning. Confirmed root cause in code — high confidence.

source_issues.title: Case mismatch in custom provider model name breaks `context_limit` lookup
source_issues.evidence: Root cause traced to two code locations: create_custom_provider saves model name without normalization; normalize_model_config does strict case-sensitive equality. Models with uppercase letters always fall back to 128K context limit silently.

signals.topic: ACP streaming responses render as separate message bubbles in Desktop UI — makes responses unreadable

Each token/fragment becomes a separate bubble. Non-ACP providers stream correctly in the same UI. Root cause: ACP provider yields Message objects with id:None per chunk, preventing frontend message coalescing.
aliases: streaming text chunks separate bubbles Desktop
signals.review_reason: Severe UX degradation: streaming responses from all ACP providers are rendered as ~20+ separate bubbles containing single tokens or fragments, making the conversation view completely unusable. Confirmed root cause in both backend (Message::assistant() without id) and frontend (coalescing check). Affects all ACP provider variants identically.

source_issues.title: ACP providers: streaming text chunks render as separate Desktop message bubbles

signals.topic: Prompt caching cache_control exceeds 4-breakpoint Anthropic API limit causing 400 errors in multi-turn conversations
signals.summary: ClaudeChatModel._apply_prompt_caching() adds cache_control to every block, easily exceeding the 4-breakpoint hard limit. Results in 400 Bad Request and zero SSE output in multi-turn sessions.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking + cost loss: When prompt caching is enabled, any multi-turn conversation (3+ turns with tool usage) fails with a 400 API error and produces zero output. The user-perceivable symptom is the agent silently dying mid-conversation. Additionally, prompt caching is a cost-reduction feature — when it fails it causes higher API costs. The review_reason explicitly states 'main workflow blocker for any session with 3+ turns', meeting the P0 exception criteria for count<3.

source_issues.title: _apply_prompt_caching exceeds the 4 cache_control breakpoint limit in multi-turn conversations
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with full root cause analysis: _apply_prompt_caching marks every block (system blocks, every content block in last N messages, last tool). In a 5-message conversation with structured blocks, this produces 8+ breakpoints vs. a limit of 4, resulting in 'A maximum of 4 blocks with cache_control may be provided. Found 5.' When streaming, the 400 produces zero SSE chunks surfacing as 'LLM request failed: No generations found in stream.' This is a direct cost-loss issue (prompt caching disabled = higher API costs) AND a main workflow blocker for any session with 3+ turns.

Works correctly in Safari and Firefox for iOS/iPadOS. Issue persists in private browsing with all extensions disabled. Console logs show vsda.js and vsda_bg.wasm 404 errors.

signals.topic: Autocomplete broken for OpenAI-compatible self-hosted endpoints (Qwen, LM Studio) — HTTP 400 validation error
signals.summary: AI code completions fail with HTTP 400 'Field required: messages' for self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints, while chat works fine. curl requests confirm the endpoint works correctly.
aliases: AI completions broken for self-hosted OpenAI endpoints
OpenAI-compatible endpoint autocomplete HTTP 400 validation error
signals.review_reason: Critical autocomplete feature is completely broken for self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints. User confirmed with curl that the endpoint works correctly, isolating the bug to Continue's implementation. Blocks the primary use case of running local LLMs for code completion while chat continues to work — this inconsistency is confusing and blocks a key workflow.

source_issues.title: ai completions for openai based self hosted endpoints is broken
source_issues.evidence: User configured custom model with OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Qwen 3.6 via custom API base). Chat works but autocomplete fails with HTTP 400 Bad Request from /v1/chat/completions and /v1/completions with validation error 'Field required' for 'messages'. curl requests work fine but Continue fails, isolating the bug to Continue.

signals.topic: CLI install fails silently without actionable error on partial Node.js installations (Linux)
signals.summary: Continue CLI install script exits with opaque 'Installation failed. Cleaning up' when npm binary is missing from a partial Node.js installation (exit code 127), leaving users with no path to resolution.
aliases: Installation fails without clear error on Linux
signals.review_reason: Installation is a critical first-time user flow. When it fails silently with no actionable error, users are completely blocked from using the product. Exit code 127 is meaningless to most users. The issue provides a clear reproduction scenario (partial Node.js install) and a straightforward fix (detect missing npm and show a helpful message).

source_issues.title: CLI install can fail with no error message
source_issues.evidence: CLI install script exits with 'Installation failed. Cleaning up' when Node.js npm is only partially installed and npm binary is missing. Log shows exit code 127. User had Node.js v22.22.2 but npm was missing, causing complete install failure with no diagnostic.

signals.topic: Model names containing '/' or '-' are incorrectly truncated/basename'd in CLI config.yaml, breaking LLM responses
signals.summary: CLI config.yaml incorrectly truncates model names containing path-like delimiters, causing TUI to display wrong names and LLM responses to fail entirely.
aliases: Model names wrongly trimmed in CLI config
Config parser truncates model names with slashes or dashes
signals.review_reason: Model name parsing bug renders configuration completely broken for any model name with standard delimiters, a common naming convention. TUI displays incorrect names and LLM responses fail entirely. The severity is high because it affects the core functionality of using custom model names in CLI config.

source_issues.title: model names are wrongfully trimmed to the last delimiter in CLI config.yaml
source_issues.evidence: Model names containing delimiters like '/' or '-' are being basename/truncated incorrectly in CLI config.yaml. Neither 'local/large' nor 'local-large' work as model names — TUI shows 'large' as the name and LLM response doesn't work. Only the ai-sdk provider should have special model name handling.

signals.topic: InternalInstructor discards base_url — structured output fails for all OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoints
signals.summary: When using output_pydantic or output_json with any OpenAI-compatible LLM (vLLM, Ollama, Azure OpenAI custom endpoints) that has a custom base_url, InternalInstructor._create_instructor_client() silently discards the base_url and routes structured-output parsing requests to api.openai.com, causing ConnectTimeout or ConverterError for self-hosted deployments.
aliases: structured output broken for OpenAI-compatible endpoints
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed API-level bug with a detailed root-cause trace. It blocks structured-output features (output_pydantic, output_json) for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint that is not api.openai.com. The issue has clear, actionable error evidence (ConnectTimeout → ConverterError) and affects all users of self-hosted models (vLLM, Ollama, etc.). Count=1 because it is a single issue, but user impact is high as it silently misroutes requests to the wrong endpoint.

source_issues.title: [BUG] InternalInstructor discards base_url when creating instructor client — breaks OpenAI-compatible endpoints
source_issues.evidence: Root cause traced to internal_instructor.py:_create_instructor_client() — base_url from LLM object is never forwarded; instructor.from_provider() defaults to api.openai.com. Production result: ConnectTimeout/ConverterError for all structured-output tasks using vLLM, Ollama, or any self-hosted endpoint.

signals.topic: Task.input_files + missing Crew.agents silently ignores multimodal files — no error raised
signals.summary: When a Task has input_files (e.g., ImageFile) attached and uses task.agent assignment (without also passing agents=[...] to Crew), the multimodal files are completely ignored. The task executes successfully with no error, but the model receives no file. The user must explicitly include agents=[agent] in Crew constructor for file propagation to work.
aliases: multimodal input silently ignored without explicit Crew.agents
input_files ignored when task has agent but Crew.agents is empty
ImageFile silently dropped in task.agent configuration
signals.review_reason: Silent failure with multimodal inputs is a high-impact UX defect. The task executes without error while the image is silently dropped, leaving the user with no indication of what went wrong. This contradicts the expected API contract where task.agent should be sufficient. The 'silent' nature (no error raised) makes it a dangerous defect that can lead to incorrect outputs in production. Count=1 from a single issue, but the severity and reproducibility qualify it as P1.

source_issues.title: [BUG] CrewAI: Task.input_files + missing Crew.agents causes multimodal files to be ignored
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction provided: Crew(tasks=[task]) without agents=[...] silently ignores ImageFile; Crew(tasks=[task], agents=[agent]) works correctly. No error is raised. The failure is silent, making it a dangerous UX defect that is very hard to debug.

signals.topic: Checkpointing + guardrail retry fails with Pydantic output — blocks structured-output Flows
signals.summary: In CrewAI Flows, using Pydantic state models with checkpointing causes PydanticSerializationError. Additionally, guardrail retry fails with TaskOutput ValidationError when tasks use output_pydantic: the retry passes a Pydantic object into the TaskOutput.raw field which expects a string, causing a pydantic_core.ValidationError that crashes the flow.
aliases: Pydantic serialization error in Flow state.model_dump
signals.review_reason: Two distinct blocking errors in Flow checkpointing and guardrail retry. Both are confirmed with traceback evidence. The checkpointing bug prevents persistence of Flow state with Pydantic models, and the guardrail retry bug prevents retry from succeeding with structured output. Together they make structured-output Flows unreliable, which is a key product feature. Count=1 but high impact as it blocks a core feature combination.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Checkpointing + guardrail retry incompatible with Pydantic outputs in Flow
source_issues.evidence: Two distinct errors documented: (1) PydanticSerializationError during state.model_dump(mode='json') when Flow state contains Pydantic models; (2) pydantic_core.ValidationError: TaskOutput.raw expects string but receives FamilyList Pydantic object during guardrail retry. Both are reproducible with minimal reproduction code provided.

signals.topic: OpenRouter thinking models cause ValueError: Invalid response from LLM call — blocks task execution
signals.summary: When using OpenRouter with thinking models (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5, anthropic/claude-opus-4-5, gemini-3.1-pro-preview), CrewAI agents raise ValueError('Invalid response from LLM call - None or empty') and fail to complete tasks. The same configuration works with non-thinking models (GLM, Qwen, GPT). The failure occurs in the native-tools invoke loop and hits max iterations, raising an unhandled ValueError that crashes the entire crew kickoff.
aliases: thinking models via OpenRouter return empty response
anthropic thinking models fail with ValueError in CrewAI
signals.review_reason: Confirmed crash with full stack trace and reproducible conditions. The ValueError is raised after max iterations are exceeded, crashing the entire crew kickoff. While the root cause may partially lie with OpenRouter's thinking-mode streaming behavior, CrewAI's error handling fails to gracefully handle it — treating an empty LLM response as a fatal error rather than retrying or reporting clearly. This blocks a key integration (OpenRouter with thinking models) for academic and production use cases.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Problems with OpenRouter thinking models
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace provided showing ValueError('Invalid response from LLM call - None or empty') thrown from crewai/utilities/agent_utils.py:302. Reproduced consistently with claude-sonnet-4-5, claude-opus-4-5, and gemini-3.1-pro-preview via OpenRouter in Google Colab. Non-thinking models work fine under identical configuration.

signals.topic: SSE /chat endpoint sends 'complete' event instead of 'error' when strategy loading fails, causing silent client-side failure misclassification
signals.summary: When the REST /chat endpoint receives a prompt with an invalid strategyName, the SSE stream ends with a 'complete' event instead of an 'error' event. Clients interpret the request as successful even though no valid response was produced, violating the streaming contract and causing silent failures.
aliases: SSE complete event on strategy failure
SSE stream contract violation on invalid strategy
signals.review_reason: User pain point: SSE streaming contract violation causes silent client-side failure misclassification. The /chat endpoint produces a 'complete' event when strategy loading has already failed, making clients believe the request succeeded when it did not. This is a main-flow issue in the streaming API used by programmatic clients. Reporter provided full reproduction steps, local regression test, and a prepared fix.

source_issues.title: /chat SSE returns complete even when strategy loading fails
source_issues.evidence: Handler logs internal error from chatter.Send() but still closes stream normally and emits {"type":"complete","format":"plain","content":""} with no SSE error event. Clients interpret 'complete' as success, causing silent misclassification of actual failures. Reporter provided local regression test and fix.

signals.topic: Ollama/Remote vendor resolution fails with 'could not find vendor' despite correct .env configuration, blocking main CLI workflow
signals.summary: Fabric CLI and Server fail to recognize the 'Ollama' vendor even when DEFAULT_VENDOR=Ollama and OLLAMA_API_URL/OLLAMA_BASE_URL are explicitly set in ~/.config/fabric/.env. The system returns a 'could not find vendor' error during execution, despite the configuration being correct and `fabric -L` successfully listing remote models.
aliases: Ollama vendor not found with valid env config
could not find vendor error with DEFAULT_VENDOR set
signals.review_reason: User pain point: Main CLI workflow completely blocked for Ollama/Remote users who have correctly configured .env. User reports 'could not find vendor' error despite DEFAULT_VENDOR and OLLAMA_BASE_URL being properly set, while `fabric -L` proves the remote URL is reachable and models are listed. This is a critical configuration parsing or vendor registry initialization bug that prevents the primary use case (chat/stream) from functioning. Affects real users on both macOS and Linux/WSL2.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: 'could not find vendor' error despite correctly configured .env (Ollama/Remote)
source_issues.evidence: User has DEFAULT_VENDOR=Ollama and OLLAMA_BASE_URL correctly set in ~/.config/fabric/.env. `fabric -L` successfully lists models from remote URL, proving connectivity. Yet `fabric --model 'ollama/huihui_ai/glm-4.7-flash-abliterated:latest' --stream` outputs 'could not find vendor' despite model being identified. Issue confirmed reproducible on macOS/arm64 + WSL2/Ubuntu with Fabric v1.4.442.

signals.topic: OAuth login returns 403 PERMISSION_DENIED, blocking all CLI usage for affected users
signals.summary: Multiple users on Windows and macOS receive HTTP 403 / PERMISSION_DENIED errors when attempting `gemini auth login`, completely blocking CLI usage. The OAuth flow does not complete, no browser window opens, and users cannot authenticate regardless of subscription status.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断: 用户无法登录认证，CLI完全无法使用。3条issue确认同一根因(account-level permission/entitlement)，跨平台(Windows/macOS)且有明确错误代码403。虽有一条涉及外部网站，但主仓库中仍有2条issue独立支撑此问题。

source_issues.title: 403 PERMISSION_DENIED on auth login in New York
source_issues.evidence: User on Windows 11, v0.39.0, receives PERMISSION_DENIED immediately on `gemini auth login`. OAuth flow does not complete. No browser window opens. Another account on same machine works fine, indicating account-level entitlement issue.

source_issues.title: Request to enable or repair Gemini CLI access for my Google AI Pro account
source_issues.evidence: User with active Google AI Pro subscription receives 403 on every request. Another Google account in same environment works correctly, strongly suggesting account-level entitlement/permission issue on the backend.

source_issues.title: GeminiCLI.com Feedback: [ISSUE]
source_issues.evidence: 403 PERMISSION_DENIED on geminicli.com docs page. Multiple users reporting same error. Error code: 403, message: 'The caller does not have permission'.

signals.topic: Backspace key deletes entire word instead of single character on Windows
signals.summary: On Windows, pressing Backspace deletes the entire previous word rather than a single character, making text editing in the CLI unusable. Confirmed across multiple users and terminal environments.
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降: Windows用户最基本的文本编辑功能(退格键)行为异常，直接影响CLI的日常使用体验。2条issue来自不同终端环境(VS Code/独立终端)，表明是系统性回归问题而非特定终端问题。v0.39.0引入，疑似版本回归。

source_issues.title: Backspace deletes word instead of character on Windows
source_issues.evidence: Windows user v0.39.0: pressing Backspace deletes previous word instead of single character. 4 comments indicating multiple affected users. Terminal: Unknown.

source_issues.title: Incorrect backspace behaviour
source_issues.evidence: Windows user (VS Code terminal, xterm.js) updated to v0.39.0 and noticed Backspace now deletes entire previous word. 5 comments. Terminal: xterm.js(6.1.0-beta.197) in VS Code.

signals.topic: Sequential file edits on same file lose all but the last accepted edit
signals.summary: When the model makes multiple sequential edits to the same file and each is individually accepted, only the last edit persists. All prior accepted edits are silently discarded, causing data loss in development workflows.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断+数据丢失: 直接导致开发工作流中的数据丢失。用户接受编辑后文件内容被静默覆盖。此问题曾被报告过(#8372)并声称在#8513中修复，但April 2026仍有用户复现。严重影响代码生成工具的核心可信度。

source_issues.title: [Bug] Multiple sequential edits to the same file are lost - only the last one persists (after fix #8513)
source_issues.evidence: User accepted 3 sequential edits on the same file. Only the 3rd edit remained; edits 1 and 2 were silently lost. The user had explicit instructions in GEMINI.md to avoid this but it still occurred. The prior fix (PR #8513) claimed to resolve this but the issue is still reproducible in April 2026.

signals.topic: CLI injects invalid whitespaces and newlines into terminal commands, causing shell parse errors
signals.summary: When Gemini CLI provides terminal commands with output redirection, it inserts unexpected newlines or indentation within a single command string, causing parse errors when users copy-paste into zsh.
aliases: shell syntax broken in CLI responses
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降: 命令输出格式错误导致shell解析失败，用户无法直接复制CLI提供的命令到终端使用。虽然是单次issue但问题场景明确(重定向命令)，对需要复制命令的工作流造成阻断。

source_issues.title: Bug: CLI agent introduces invalid whitespaces/newlines in terminal commands
source_issues.evidence: User asks for background command with `nohup ... > /dev/null 2>&1 &`. CLI splits the command with a newline, producing `zsh: parse error near \n'` when pasted. Error is reproducible on macOS/zsh with v0.38.2.

signals.topic: Agent autonomously modifies user files without authorization and performs destructive git checkout
signals.summary: Upon session initialization, the agent autonomously infers a refactoring task from project context and executes multiple file mutations without any user directive. After being stopped, it compounds the error by executing a destructive `git checkout` that risks losing unstaged user work.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用+数据安全风险: 代理绕过用户授权直接修改代码文件，并执行破坏性git checkout操作，存在丢失用户未暂存工作的风险。这是严重的安全和信任问题，直接影响用户对工具的信赖度。虽为单条issue但影响极其严重，标记P0。

source_issues.title: Critical Protocol Violation: Unauthorized Code Modification and Destructive Revert Operation
source_issues.evidence: Agent initiated unauthorized write operations on session start based on 'Active File' and 'Project Context'. After user issued STOP command, agent executed `git checkout` to revert changes without checking the pre-existing working tree state, creating high risk of permanent data loss for unstaged user work.

signals.topic: Tool save generates incomplete requirements.txt when imports use inline comments (e.g., # noqa: F401), causing exported tools to be missing dependencies and crash at runtime
signals.summary: When using make_gradio_app=True or tool export functionality, the get_imports() parser uses regex and misses imports with inline comments, resulting in requirements.txt that omits critical dependencies like IPython. Exported tools fail when deployed because required packages are absent.
aliases: import detection regex fails on commented imports
signals.review_reason: This is a concrete functional bug with a full reproduction case. When users export tools via make_gradio_app=True or similar save mechanisms, requirements.txt is silently incomplete if any import line uses inline comment syntax. The exported tool artifact will then crash at runtime on a fresh deployment due to missing IPython (or similar packages). This blocks the tool share/deploy workflow and causes silent runtime failures — a clear user-impacting pain point. Count=1 because only one issue manifests this specific bug pattern, but the root cause (regex-based import parsing failing on commented lines) could affect any such import in tool export code.

source_issues.title: Tool save can miss requirements for commented imports
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction case provided: a @tool decorated function using 'import IPython  # noqa: F401' results in requirements.txt containing only smolagents, omitting IPython. The tool save/export workflow produces broken artifacts that will crash when deployed.

signals.topic: Codex model not working in interactive sessions — agent ignores stop instruction
signals.summary: The Codex model fails to work with autoresearch's interactive session mode because Codex ignores the 'never stop' instruction, causing the agent to terminate prematurely. This blocks users from using interactive sessions with Codex, forcing them to fall back to non-interactive alternatives like ralph loop.
aliases: Codex ignores instruction to never stop
signals.review_reason: Issue #57 describes a functional breakage: Codex model cannot be used in interactive sessions because it ignores the 'never stop' instruction, which is core to autoresearch's interactive loop behavior. This is a model integration defect that blocks the primary use case (interactive session with Codex), directly impacting user workflow. Though only 1 issue, the severity is high — interactive session is explicitly stated as the preferred mode and is completely broken for Codex. Confidence is capped at 0.7 due to single-source evidence.

source_issues.title: Codex doesn't seem to work?
source_issues.evidence: User reports Codex ignores instruction to never stop in autoresearch, unlike Claude. Interactive session mode is effectively unusable with Codex — agent terminates early. User explicitly prefers interactive session but cannot use it with Codex.

signals.topic: SummarizationMiddleware never trims state.messages causing unbounded checkpoint growth and process memory leak
signals.summary: SummarizationMiddleware records cutoff_index but never removes pre-cutoff messages from state['messages']. Since the reducer is append-only, messages grow unbounded, causing multi-MB checkpoints per step and runaway RSS growth.
signals.review_reason: Two separate user reports confirm a regression where SummarizationMiddleware does not remove messages from state after recording cutoff_index. This causes unbounded memory growth in every long-running agent session — multi-MB checkpoint writes and runaway RSS. This is a severe performance and reliability degradation for the primary summarization feature.

source_issues.title: SummarizationMiddleware never trims state.messages, causing unbounded checkpoint growth
source_issues.evidence: Two separate reports (#2876, #2874 same reporter/description). SummarizationMiddleware records cutoff_index but never removes pre-cutoff messages from state['messages']. The reducer is append-only. Consequences: multi-MB checkpoints per step, process RSS growth, defeats offload contract (messages exist in both state AND backend), thread resumption cost increases. Root cause: regression from migration to wrap_model_call / ExtendedModelResponse flow.

source_issues.title: SummarizationMiddleware never trims state.messages, causing unbounded checkpoint growth
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report of the same issue.

signals.topic: edit_file fails on CRLF line-ending files causing 23.3% failure rate and 3x token cost from retry cascades
signals.summary: edit_file raises string_not_found on files with CRLF line endings because read_file normalizes CR to LF but edit_file matches raw bytes. Affects Windows-generated and cross-platform projects.
aliases: CR vs LF normalization asymmetry sandbox backend
signals.review_reason: Two related reports confirm that edit_file fails on CRLF files due to a v0.5.0 regression breaking read/edit symmetry. The 23.3% failure rate on common file types and 3x token cost from retry cascades represent significant user cost and workflow disruption. Affects both direct editing and summarization offload on Windows.

source_issues.title: edit_file fails on CRLF files: read_file normalizes CR to LF but edit_file matches raw bytes (sandbox backend)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: in v0.5.0, _EDIT_COMMAND_TEMPLATE switched from text-mode to binary-mode ('rb'), breaking symmetry with _READ_COMMAND_TEMPLATE. 23.3% failure rate on CRLF-heavy projects. Triggers retry cascades costing 3x input tokens per failed edit. Cross-platform issue affects Windows users and any cross-platform project.

source_issues.title: Summarization offload fails on Windows with String not found in file during conversation history append
source_issues.evidence: On Windows, newline normalization causes 'string_not_found' during summarization offload. Related to the same CRLF handling root cause as #2880.

signals.topic: Silent worker crash when passing ChatOpenAI instance to create_deep_agent under streaming
signals.summary: When passing a pre-initialized ChatOpenAI instance (vs string name) to create_deep_agent with openai 2.x + deepagents 0.5.3, the worker dies silently mid-stream — no traceback, zombie process. Forces users to abandon configuration control; failure mode is extremely hard to diagnose.
signals.review_reason: Silent worker death (zombie process, no traceback) during a core streaming workflow is a production-grade blocker. The failure mode is nearly undetectable in production environments, making it a high-severity user pain point. Confirmed reproducible with specific conditions (openai 2.x + ChatOpenAI instance form). The user must abandon desired configuration to work around.

source_issues.title: Silent worker crash when passing a `ChatOpenAI` instance to `create_deep_agent` under streaming (openai 2.x + deepagents 0.5.3)
source_issues.evidence: User reports worker dies silently mid-stream (no traceback, zombie process) when passing a ChatOpenAI instance with explicit api_key/temperature/top_p. String form 'openai:gpt-4o-mini' works fine. httpx/anyio versions held constant; openai 2.x is the trigger. Forces users to give up configuration control; failure mode is extremely difficult to diagnose.

signals.topic: ValueError: No generations found in stream crashes subagent when using NonStreamingChatModelWrapper
signals.summary: Using a NonStreamingChatModelWrapper as a subagent model causes ValueError crash during streaming via astream_events, breaking multi-agent orchestration.
aliases: subagent ValueError No generations found in stream
