signals.review_reason: Agent workflow completely crashes with a ValueError when a subagent uses a non-streaming model wrapper. Full stack trace provided with reproducible code. This is a direct main-flow blocker for multi-agent setups, which are a core use case of deepagents. User impact is severe — the entire agent run fails.

source_issues.title: ValueError: No generations found in stream
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace provided. When using NonStreamingChatModelWrapper as a subagent model, the streaming pipeline raises ValueError: No generations found in stream. The error propagates through langchain_core streaming infrastructure. User provides minimal reproducible example with create_deep_agent and subagents configuration.

signals.topic: CompositeBackend route isolation leaks across shared storage backends causing silent data corruption
signals.summary: Files written to one CompositeBackend route silently leak into other routes during grep/ls/glob operations when backends share the same underlying BaseStore.
signals.review_reason: Silent data corruption — a file written in one route scope appears in grep/ls results of other routes. This is a correctness failure that can cause agents to act on wrong data, leading to incorrect outputs or actions. The root cause is clearly identified by the reporter and affects common multi-route usage patterns.

source_issues.title: CompositeBackend route isolation leaks across shared storage backends
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: route prefix stripping happens before delegation to backends, but all backends return full unscoped result sets. Example: comp.grep('content', path='/') returns paths from ALL routes, not just the matched route. Affects grep, ls, and glob operations. Silent data corruption in common patterns where a single InMemoryStore is shared across routes.

signals.topic: MIME type silently hard-coded to 'application/pdf' for non-PDF files attached via OpenAI base64 block shape
signals.summary: In langchain_core message translation, the file branch of _convert_openai_format_to_data_block hard-codes mime_type='application/pdf' regardless of the actual file type. CSV, JSON, text, and Office documents attached via the OpenAI prescribed base64 block shape are silently mislabeled as PDFs. This propagates wrong MIME types to all downstream integrations consuming content_blocks.
signals.review_reason: Silent data corruption that breaks file-type-dependent downstream integrations. Any user attaching CSV, text, or Office files via the documented OpenAI base64 block shape gets silently wrong MIME types. This is not an edge case — it affects every non-PDF file attachment path. Two independent reporters confirm the same bug.

source_issues.title: core: _convert_openai_format_to_data_block hard-codes mime_type on base64 file blocks
source_issues.evidence: Repro passes data:text/csv;base64,... via OpenAI block shape; resulting content_block has mime_type='application/pdf' instead of 'text/csv'. The image branch already correctly reads from the data URI.

source_issues.title: core: _convert_openai_format_to_data_block hard-codes mime_type="application/pdf" on base64 file blocks
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #36939, same bug. Verified as same root cause from separate reporter.

signals.topic: Compaction feature causes Anthropic API BadRequestError with streaming modes in agent workflows
signals.summary: Using compaction beta with print_mode='messages' or stream_mode='messages' causes LangChain to pass an 'index' field from streaming blocks into the Anthropic API request, triggering BadRequestError: 'Extra inputs are not permitted'. Agent workflows with long context become unusable after the first compaction trigger.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocker: compaction is a core context-management feature, and its interaction with streaming modes causes agents to crash deterministically after token threshold is crossed. Users with long-context agent workflows cannot rely on compaction as documented. Strong evidence: full stack trace, minimal reproducible script, clear root cause in _format_messages.

source_issues.title: Using compaction causes Anthropic's API to fail when agent invoked with print_mode="messages" or when streaming with stream_mode="messages"
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible crash: after compaction triggers, the streaming 'index' field leaks into the next Anthropic API call, producing BadRequestError. User provides minimal repro script. Same index-field issue seen with custom tools after compaction.

signals.topic: create_agent with checkpointing returns stale structured_response on subsequent turns causing premature exit
signals.summary: When using create_agent with response_format and a checkpointer, the structured_response from turn N is restored into state at turn N+1, and routing edges check 'structured_response in state' as an exit condition. This causes the agent to exit before the model runs, returning stale data from the previous turn instead of a fresh answer.
signals.review_reason: Main-flow data corruption in multi-turn agent sessions with checkpointing: users see wrong answers returned silently. The structured_response from a previous turn is treated as valid for the current turn, bypassing the model call entirely. Identified by clear root cause in source code and reproducible minimal example.

source_issues.title: `create_agent`: stale `structured_response` from checkpoint causes premature exit on next turn
source_issues.evidence: Minimal repro shows turn 2 returns Answer(text='Hi') from turn 1 instead of the fresh Answer(text='Bye') from turn 2. Root cause identified in factory.py routing edges. Reproduces on main branch.

signals.topic: Agent default max recursion limit of 9999 causes runaway token consumption and significant financial loss
signals.summary: The agent's default max recursion is set to 9999 (renamed from 10000). The documentation does not explain this limit. When agents enter runaway loops, they consume thousands of API calls and tokens without user consent, resulting in direct financial costs. One reporter documents $800 in losses in a single afternoon.
signals.review_reason: Explicitly documented financial harm: $800 in direct API costs from runaway recursion. While count=1, the severity and specificity of the financial evidence (LangSmith trace + explicit dollar amount) make this a P0. The default limit of 9999 is undocumented and directly caused token-hungry runaway behavior.

source_issues.title: 兄弟，agent默认递归次数是9_999？文档里也从未交代，一下午浪费我800元，你要坑死我？
source_issues.evidence: User reports losing $800 in API costs due to the 9999 recursion limit without documentation. LangSmith trace provided. Explicit complaint: '一下午浪费我800元' (wasted 800 yuan in one afternoon). Related to langgraph issue #7313.

signals.topic: Multi-turn structured output fails with ValueError when assistant response is appended to conversation context
signals.summary: When using with_structured_output() and appending a prior assistant response (serialized via model_dump_json) to the message history for a subsequent call, the second invoke() raises ValueError because the response has 'parsed=None' and 'refusal=None'. The bug only manifests in multi-turn setups where prior responses are added back as assistant messages.
signals.review_reason: Blocks multi-turn agent workflows that use structured output with message history — a common RAG and agentic pattern. The ValueError is a clear crash with full stack trace and reproducible minimal example. The workaround (change role to 'user') is non-obvious and users would not discover it independently.

source_issues.title: Structured Output Fails When Appending Assistant Response to Context
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace showing ValueError: Structured Output response does not have a 'parsed' field nor a 'refusal' field. Repro: call structured_llm.invoke(), append serialized response as 'assistant' role message, call again — fails with ValueError. Works if role changed to 'user'.

signals.topic: BinaryOperatorAggregate silently drops values after Overwrite in same superstep
signals.summary: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update() has a guard that silently discards regular channel values arriving after an Overwrite in the same batch, with no error or warning. This causes deterministic data corruption in concurrent supersteps.
signals.review_reason: Clear data loss bug where concurrent writes in the same superstep are silently discarded depending on path-based ordering. This is not an edge case - it happens deterministically in normal concurrent graph execution. No error is raised, so users get wrong state without knowing. 2 separate users reported this issue independently.

source_issues.title: bug: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update() silently drops values arriving after Overwrite
source_issues.evidence: In concurrent supersteps, task write ordering within apply_writes is determined by path sorting, not user intent. If Task A writes Overwrite(base) and Task B writes regular value, and A sorts first, Task B's value is silently lost. No error, no warning.

source_issues.title: BinaryOperatorAggregate silently drops regular values that appear after an Overwrite
source_issues.evidence: When multiple nodes write to channel in same super-step and values array contains Overwrite followed by subsequent regular values, the subsequent regular values are silently dropped with no warning or error. Should raise InvalidUpdateError.

signals.topic: Checkpointer branching regressions break time-travel and fork workflow
signals.summary: Two regression bugs since version 1.1.7 that break the core time-travel and branching functionality: forking via checkpoint_id produces duplicate messages, and second regenerate fails to create sibling branch.
signals.review_reason: Two related regression bugs that break core time-travel and branching functionality. Issue 7592 is a clear regression from PR #7498 affecting the regenerate (time-travel) workflow. Issue 7593 is another branching bug with checkpointer interaction. Both affect the main branching/forking workflow which is fundamental to LangGraph's state management.

source_issues.title: Agent with checkpointer=True: forking human message produces duplicate human messages in new branch
source_issues.evidence: Forking a human message via checkpoint_id produces BOTH original and forked message instead of only new one. Affects version 1.1.9. Workaround of checkpointer=False hits separate regression #7592.

source_issues.title: Regression in 1.1.7 (#7498): Second regenerate from latest checkpoint doesn't create new branch
source_issues.evidence: Since 1.1.7, calling astream twice with same parent checkpoint_id fails to create second sibling branch. Works on 1.1.6, broken on 1.1.7+. Third consecutive time-travel silently overwrites instead of creating new branch.

signals.topic: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes caches INTERRUPT/ERROR writes bypassing retry logic
signals.summary: SyncPregelLoop is missing a guard that the async version has, causing failed/interrupted tasks' error writes to be cached and replayed as valid results, completely bypassing RetryPolicy.
signals.review_reason: Cache policy correctness bug where failed/interrupted tasks have their error writes cached and replayed on subsequent invocations, bypassing retry logic entirely. The async path already has the fix, showing this is a known pattern that was overlooked in the sync path. Users relying on CachePolicy would get silent failures instead of retries.

source_issues.title: bug: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes caches INTERRUPT/ERROR writes (async path already guarded)
source_issues.evidence: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes is missing guard that async version has. When using sync API with CachePolicy, a task that fails or is interrupted has error writes cached. Next invocation replays those writes as valid result, bypassing retry logic.

signals.topic: ToolNode._arun_one blocks event loop when using sync wrap_tool_call
signals.summary: ToolNode falls back to calling sync wrap_tool_call directly on the event loop thread, serializing all concurrent tool executions and stalling the event loop for async applications.
signals.review_reason: Breaks concurrent async tool execution by serializing all tool calls when using sync wrap_tool_call. Event loop blocking is a significant degradation for async applications. Users using ainvoke with multiple concurrent tools will see sequential execution instead of parallel.

source_issues.title: bug: ToolNode._arun_one blocks event loop when using sync wrap_tool_call
source_issues.evidence: ToolNode._arun_one falls back to calling sync wrap_tool_call directly on event loop thread when no async variant is provided. Since _afunc dispatches all tool calls via asyncio.gather, a single blocking sync wrapper serializes every concurrent tool execution and stalls the event loop.

signals.topic: TAG_NOSTREAM inconsistency - LLM tokens suppressed but node output messages still stream
signals.summary: StreamMessagesHandler handles TAG_NOSTREAM inconsistently: on_chat_model_start respects it but on_chain_start does not, causing node output messages to leak while LLM tokens are suppressed.
signals.review_reason: TAG_NOSTREAM tag works for LLM tokens but not node output messages, creating inconsistent behavior. This breaks per-subagent streaming control for frameworks built on LangGraph. The proposed fix is one line but the impact affects downstream frameworks like Deep Agents.

source_issues.title: `TAG_NOSTREAM` inconsistency in `StreamMessagesHandler`: suppresses LLM tokens but not node output messages
source_issues.evidence: on_chat_model_start checks TAG_NOSTREAM and skips LLM token recording correctly. But on_chain_start only checks TAG_HIDDEN, NOT TAG_NOSTREAM - node output messages still stream. Affects frameworks built on LangGraph (Deep Agents) that need per-subagent streaming control.

signals.topic: RAG Knowledge Retrieval Returns Empty Results
signals.summary: When testing knowledge base retrieval, users consistently get empty/null results even when the queried text exists in indexed documents. Multiple retrieval strategy adjustments (TopK, score threshold, weighting modes) fail to surface the expected segments.
signals.review_reason: Core RAG functionality is broken: users cannot retrieve content they have explicitly indexed. This blocks the primary use case of knowledge-based Q&A. While count=1, the severity is P0 because it completely defeats the knowledge retrieval pipeline — the central value proposition of Dify's RAG system.

source_issues.title: Retrieval Test return the "null"
source_issues.evidence: User has a chunk containing '修改教材', yet the recall test consistently yields no results. User experimented with all available retrieval strategies — empty results regardless of mode, TopK, or score threshold adjustments.

signals.topic: Reset Password Triggers Internal Server Error (500) on Self-Hosted Deployments
signals.summary: Users on self-hosted Docker deployments receive an immediate HTTP 500 Internal Server Error when attempting to use the 'Forgot your password?' feature. The error is a SQLAlchemy DetachedInstanceError in the account service layer.
signals.review_reason: Authentication flow is completely broken: users cannot reset their own passwords on self-hosted instances. This is a hard blocker for user self-service and forces manual admin intervention. Full traceback and clear reproduction steps confirm a real SQLAlchemy session management bug in the password reset code path.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Internal Server Error when using Reset Password feature
source_issues.evidence: On Dify 1.13.1 self-hosted Docker, clicking 'Forgot your password?' immediately throws Internal Server Error. Full traceback shows sqlalchemy.orm.exc.DetachedInstanceError in account_service.py:send_reset_password_email. Users cannot recover their accounts.

signals.topic: Human Input Node Streaming API Returns Empty Data Payload, Breaking External Integration
signals.summary: When calling the Dify Open API endpoint /v1/chat-messages with streaming mode, the 'human_input_required' event returns only the event name with a completely empty data body — missing form_content, form_token, and action button configurations. The web frontend preview works correctly.
aliases: human input node SSE event missing data
workflow approval integration broken via API
signals.review_reason: This breaks the primary integration contract for Human-in-the-loop workflows via the public API. External systems cannot receive form data or form tokens to resume workflows. This directly blocks enterprise automation scenarios that depend on Dify's Open API for approval workflows.

source_issues.title: Workflow Human Input human_input_required event returns empty data in Open API streaming call
source_issues.evidence: API returns {"event":"human_input_required"} with empty data. Web preview returns complete payload. External systems cannot obtain approval information or resume the workflow — the Human Input node's entire purpose in automated flows is defeated.

signals.topic: Copy Button UI Feedback Never Updates After Clicking
signals.summary: The shared useClipboard hook never flips the 'copied' state to true after a successful copy operation. As a result, the copy icon tooltip stays on 'Copy' forever and never shows 'Copied', and the icon never changes from outline to filled. Secondary issue: CopyFeedback also clears the state on mouse leave.
aliases: copy icon stuck on pre-copy state
signals.review_reason: Clear UI bug with identified root cause in shared hook code. However, it does not block any primary workflow — it is purely cosmetic feedback. Downgraded to P2 because the impact is limited to copy confirmation UX, not functional failure.

source_issues.title: Bug: Copy button tooltip never switches to 'Copied' after clicking
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified in code: useClipboard hook awaits writeTextToClipboard but never calls handleCopyResult(true) on success. CopyFeedback also has onMouseLeave=reset clearing state instantly. Affects all callers including the Service API endpoint copy on /datasets page.

signals.topic: Embedded Chatbot Always Prioritizes localStorage conversation_id Over URL Parameter
signals.summary: The embedded chatbot's useMemo hook prioritizes conversationIdInfo from localStorage over the conversation_id URL parameter. Once localStorage has a stored conversation ID from any prior interaction, passing a different conversation_id via embed.js has no effect — the parent website cannot switch conversations or start new ones programmatically.
aliases: conversation_id not switchable in embedded mode
signals.review_reason: This prevents programmatic conversation switching in embedded deployments — a common enterprise use case. The bug is confirmed with a clear root cause in React hook code. Downgraded to P1 (not P0) because it does not block core functionality, only the ability to control conversation context from the parent page.

source_issues.title: Embedded chatbot ignores URL conversation_id parameter when localStorage has a stored value
source_issues.evidence: Root cause in web/app/components/base/chat/embedded-chatbot/hooks.tsx: localStorage priority always wins over URL param. Three related issues (#33362, #34731, #35489) all share this root cause. Parent websites cannot control which conversation is loaded via embed.js.

signals.topic: v2 ADD-only pipeline missing semantic conflict resolution: contradictory facts both stored instead of producing UPDATE
signals.summary: The v2 ADD-only pipeline only does MD5 hash deduplication. Adding contradictory facts like 'my name is Alice' then 'my name is Bob' stores both as separate ADD events instead of an UPDATE, degrading retrieval quality.
signals.review_reason: Data quality degradation: documentation promises semantic conflict resolution but implementation only does hash dedup. Contradictory facts both stored, degrading retrieval accuracy. Affects any multi-session user updating facts.

source_issues.title: Semantic conflict resolution missing in v2 pipeline
source_issues.evidence: Doc promises 'latest truth wins when contradictions detected' but implementation only does MD5 hash dedup. Adding contradictory facts stores both as separate ADD events instead of UPDATE.

source_issues.title: Conflict resolution issue (duplicate of #4904)
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #4904, same semantic conflict resolution issue reported by separate user.

signals.topic: v3 migration breaks self-hosting on Qdrant: auto-recall threshold hardcoded, native deps mis-bundled, history writes diverted
signals.summary: v3 migration causes three compounding bugs on Qdrant-backed self-host: auto-recall hook ignores searchThreshold (hardcoded 0.6/0.5 floors), native deps are bundled breaking runtime resolution, and resolvePath silently rewrites historyDbPath. The plugin silently becomes non-functional with 'no memories returned' symptoms.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: plugin silently non-functional on default Qdrant-backed self-host after v3 migration. Three root causes stack — threshold floor ignores user config, native deps break at runtime, history writes diverted to wrong path. Users cannot distinguish configuration error from bug. Count=1 prevents P0 under hard constraint but impact is clearly blocking.

source_issues.title: v3 migration breaks self-host on Qdrant: auto-recall threshold ignored, history writes diverted, native deps mis-bundled
source_issues.evidence: Three compounding bugs stack to cause 'no memories returned' and empty entity collection. Legitimate matches scoring 0.35-0.55 are dropped by 0.6 floor. Plugin silently non-functional after upgrade from 0.2.0->1.0.10 and mem0ai 2.x->3.0.1.

signals.topic: Docker image missing linux/amd64 manifest entry, preventing container from running on standard Linux x64
signals.summary: Docker pull fails on linux/amd64 due to missing manifest, blocking container deployment.
signals.review_reason: Deployment blocker: users cannot run the Docker container on standard Linux AMD64. Clear infrastructure incompatibility preventing first-time setup and deployment.

source_issues.title: Docker manifest missing linux/amd64
source_issues.evidence: Users cannot pull or run the Docker container on Linux AMD64 infrastructure. Clear deployment blocker.

signals.topic: Demo app crashes with undefined property error on memory data, preventing interactive memory visualization
signals.summary: Demo application page fails to load due to undefined property on memory data, breaking the interactive demo experience.
signals.review_reason: UX degradation: demo application crashes on page load, preventing users from evaluating mem0 interactively. Clear UX failure reproducible through documented quickstart path.

source_issues.title: Demo app broken: undefined property error on memory data
source_issues.evidence: Interactive memory demo application fails to load with undefined property error. Reproducible via quickstart demo.

signals.topic: Reasoning model extractors return empty results because mem0 reads empty 'content' field while facts reside in 'reasoning_content'
signals.summary: When using reasoning models (glm-5.1, gemma3, qwen3-vl), mem0 reads the empty content field and ignores reasoning_content where actual facts are stored, causing silent extraction failures.
signals.review_reason: Core extraction silently fails for reasoning model users: obvious facts not stored because reasoning_content field is never read. Users receive empty results with no error signal, making debugging impossible. Key feature (memory storage) non-functional for reasoning model users.

source_issues.title: Reasoning model extractor returns empty results
source_issues.evidence: When using reasoning models, content is empty and reasoning_content has the facts. Mem0 reads content only, gets empty string, silently fails with results=[] for obvious facts. Users cannot distinguish 'no new facts' from 'extraction failed'.

signals.topic: Sample documentation and configuration issues preventing beginner onboarding
signals.summary: Eight separate documentation/config issues across hosting samples prevent beginners from running samples: missing README, missing env templates, missing requirements.txt, broken venv on Windows, config mismatches between templates and code.
signals.review_reason: Nine distinct documentation/config defects across hosting samples prevent beginners from evaluating the framework via official samples. Issues range from missing files (requirements.txt, .env.example) to active misconfigurations (wrong env var names in templates). While not blocking core framework usage, these create significant onboarding friction and prevent fair product evaluation.

source_issues.title: Python: [Samples][Python] 04-hosting/ directory missing top-level README to orient beginners
source_issues.evidence: No top-level README in 04-hosting/ directory — beginners must open each subdirectory to understand available hosting options.

source_issues.title: Python: [Samples][Python] azure_functions & durabletask READMEs need quick-install commands for prerequisites
source_issues.evidence: azure_functions and durabletask READMEs list prerequisites but don't provide quick-install commands. Azure Functions Core Tools and Azurite storage emulator not found when beginners follow docs.

source_issues.title: Python: [Samples][Python] `python -m venv` hangs on Windows — READMEs should recommend uv or document workaround
source_issues.evidence: Sample READMEs recommend `python -m venv .venv` which hangs indefinitely on Windows with Microsoft Store Python 3.13 during ensurepip. Beginners get stuck at the first step.

source_issues.title: Python: [Samples][Python] durabletask/ samples missing .env.example files
source_issues.evidence: None of the 7 durabletask/ samples provide .env.example or .env.template. Users must read README or source code to discover which environment variables are needed.

source_issues.title: Python: [Samples][Python] Inconsistent config template naming across azure_functions samples (.template vs .sample vs .example)
source_issues.evidence: azure_functions samples use three different naming conventions (.template, .sample, .example) for config templates, causing beginner confusion about which file to copy.

source_issues.title: Python: [Samples][Python] azure_functions/02_multi_agent — config template and requirements.txt mismatch (Foundry vs OpenAI)
source_issues.evidence: Config template has FOUNDRY_* environment variables but code uses OpenAIChatCompletionClient which reads AZURE_OPENAI_* variables. Beginners configure wrong env vars and the sample fails silently.

source_issues.title: Python: [Samples][Python] durabletask/02_multi_agent requirements.txt references wrong package (foundry instead of openai)
source_issues.evidence: durabletask/02_multi_agent uses OpenAIChatCompletionClient but requirements.txt references packages/foundry instead of packages/openai. Misleading and could break if transitive dependencies change.

source_issues.title: Python: [Samples][Python] redis package missing from requirements.txt in streaming samples
source_issues.evidence: azure_functions/03_reliable_streaming and durabletask/03_single_agent_streaming both import redis.asyncio but redis is not listed in requirements.txt. pip install from requirements and run fails at import.

source_issues.title: Python: [Samples][Python] a2a/ sample missing requirements.txt — beginners cannot install dependencies
source_issues.evidence: The a2a/ sample has no requirements.txt file. Unlike all other samples, beginners cannot pip install dependencies. README recommends `uv run` which only works from the repo root.

signals.topic: FoundryChatClient runtime errors and missing async context manager prevent core API calls
signals.summary: FoundryChatClient fails on API calls with ChatClientException (AF 1.1) and does not implement __aenter__/__aexit__, breaking both runtime usage and the official sample code.
signals.review_reason: Two distinct but related failures on the same component: (1) ChatClientException thrown on every API call in AF 1.1, blocking core usage; (2) async context manager protocol not implemented, breaking official sample code. Both are main flow failures with clear user impact.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: AF 1.1 call FoundryChatclient report Error.
source_issues.evidence: User sets FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT and FOUNDRY_MODEL correctly but ChatClientException is raised when making API calls. Error originates in _handle_request_error in agent_framework_openai._chat_client.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: FoundryChatClient doesn't support async with, built_in_chat_clients sample fails
source_issues.evidence: FoundryChatClient does not implement __aenter__/__aexit__ methods. The built-in chat clients official sample fails with TypeError when using 'async with client:', demonstrating both a runtime gap and broken documentation.

signals.topic: ImportError: cannot import BaseContextProvider from agent_framework when using agent_framework_azure_ai
signals.summary: Users cannot import the agent_framework_azure_ai package due to a version mismatch — BaseContextProvider referenced in azure-ai package does not exist in agent-framework 1.1.1.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocker — users cannot import agent_framework_azure_ai at all due to a missing export in agent-framework 1.1.1, completely preventing use of Foundry evaluators.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: ImportError: cannot import name 'BaseContextProvider' from 'agent_framework' when importing agent_framework_azure_ai
source_issues.evidence: ImportError at runtime when users try to import FoundryEvals from agent_framework_azure_ai. agent-framework-azure-ai depends on BaseContextProvider which does not exist in agent-framework 1.1.1, preventing any use of Foundry evaluators.

signals.topic: FoundryChatClient and FoundryAgent default_headers parameter silently ignored
signals.summary: The documented default_headers parameter is accepted and stored but never forwarded to the underlying AsyncOpenAI client, making it a no-op with no error or warning.
signals.review_reason: Significant developer experience degradation — a documented API parameter is completely non-functional with no error or warning, and users waste hours debugging. May also cause cost/security issues if custom auth headers are required.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: FoundryChatClient(default_headers=...) and FoundryAgent(default_headers=...) silently drop custom headers
source_issues.evidence: default_headers parameter is accepted and stored but never passed to the underlying AsyncOpenAI client. User spent hours debugging why their custom auth/tracing headers never arrived at the API.

signals.topic: Missing /liveness health endpoint blocks hosted agent deployments
signals.summary: The hosted agent server provides /readiness but not /liveness, causing 404 errors in hosted deployments that require Kubernetes-style liveness probes.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocker for hosted/deployment scenarios — users cannot deploy hosted agents to managed hosting environments that enforce liveness probes. Prevents production deployment entirely.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Foundry Hosted Agents - Missing /liveness route while /readiness exists
source_issues.evidence: GET /liveness returns 404 in hosted agent deployments. Hosted Kubernetes-style environments require liveness probes to keep containers alive. Only /readiness exists which returns 200, but that is not sufficient for liveness checks.

signals.topic: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing — arbitrary code execution risk
signals.summary: The LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor writes LLM-generated code to disk and executes it as a subprocess via asyncio.create_subprocess_exec with no sandboxing, filesystem isolation, or network restrictions. The only safeguard is a UserWarning that can be silently filtered in production. This allows indirect prompt injection to achieve full host system compromise.
signals.review_reason: This is a concrete, verifiable security vulnerability with a defined attack scenario (indirect prompt injection → arbitrary code execution with host privileges). Not a theoretical proposal — the vulnerable code path (local/__init__.py:391-434) is explicitly identified. The safeguard (UserWarning) is proven insufficient because it can be silenced in standard production configurations (-W ignore, log pipelines). Impact is severe: credential theft, lateral movement, data destruction. Meets the threshold for P0 given the critical nature of arbitrary code execution on the host.

source_issues.title: [Security] LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing
source_issues.evidence: UserWarning at __init__.py:163-168 is the only safeguard and can be suppressed via -W ignore in production. LLM-generated code written to disk via f.write(code) then executed via asyncio.create_subprocess_exec with full host privileges. OWASP AGENT-026 / ASI-09. Attacker can exfiltrate SSH keys, cloud credentials, environment variables. Reported by agent-audit security scanner.

signals.topic: MCP tool integration lacks cryptographic identity and message integrity — tool poisoning and replay attack risk
signals.summary: AutoGen's MCP integration provides no cryptographic agent identity, no message signing, no tool definition integrity, and no replay protection. Tool definitions from tools/list are unsigned, enabling OWASP MCP03 tool poisoning attacks. JSON-RPC messages can be modified in transit without detection.
signals.review_reason: While only one issue, the MCP tool poisoning attack vector is a well-documented OWASP MCP Top 10 category with a specific CWE mapping. In AutoGen's multi-agent context, an attacker who poisons a tool definition can cause all agents using that MCP tool to execute unintended operations. The lack of message signing means parameters can be modified in transit, enabling parameter injection attacks. An IETF Internet-Draft with reference implementations exists, confirming this is a recognized industry gap with concrete mitigations available. The severity justifies P0 despite single-issue count because the attack surface is structural to AutoGen's MCP integration.

source_issues.title: MCP tool integration has no per-message authentication or integrity verification
source_issues.evidence: No agent passport or certificate mechanism for agents calling MCP tools. JSON-RPC messages are unsigned — parameters modifiable in transit. Tool definitions from tools/list are not signed, enabling OWASP MCP03 tool poisoning. No replay protection — same tool call can be replayed indefinitely. Referenced IETF draft and mcp-secure reference implementation (npm/PyPI, zero dependencies).

signals.topic: 浏览器安装时因自签名证书导致企业网络用户无法下载 Chromium（阻断安装）
signals.summary: 在企业/受限网络环境下，运行 playwright.ps1 install 或 playwright install 时，因 SSL/TLS 证书链中存在自签名证书（self-signed certificate in certificate chain）而完全无法下载 Chromium 浏览器，导致 Playwright 安装流程彻底阻断。
aliases: playwright install SSL certificate error enterprise
browser download blocked by corporate proxy certificate
signals.review_reason: 企业网络用户完全无法完成 Playwright 安装，属于主流程阻断。两条独立 issue 均提供了明确的错误信息和用户环境证据，且均出现在企业/受限网络典型场景中。自签名证书问题已有明确 stack trace 证据（SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN），足以认定用户影响。

source_issues.title: [Docs]: Workaround or url/port that needs to be unblocked to allow playwright browser install
source_issues.evidence: 运行 .\playwright.ps1 install 时报 'Error: self-signed certificate in certificate chain'，无法下载 Chrome for Testing，企业 IT 要求提供可白名单的 IP/端口。

source_issues.title: [BUG] Unable to Install because of self-signed certificate in certificate chain error is blocked by company security
source_issues.evidence: 以管理员权限运行 .\playwright.ps1 install 时收到 'Self-signed certificate in certificate chain' 错误，浏览器下载失败，用户寻求解决方案。

signals.topic: Playwright Docker 镜像与 npm 包版本不同步导致 CI 环境启动失败（Executable doesn't exist）
signals.summary: 当使用 mcr.microsoft.com/playwright Docker 镜像时，如果 npm 包版本（如 @playwright/test 1.59.1）与 Docker 镜像版本（如 v1.59.1-noble）不严格匹配，会导致 'Executable doesn't exist' 错误，CI 流水线失败。
aliases: docker image version mismatch chromium executable missing
chromium_headless_shell executable not found after version bump
signals.review_reason: CI/CD 流水线失败是主流程阻断场景。issue 提供了完整的错误输出和版本对比证据，错误信息明确指出 Executable doesn't exist，用户无法运行任何测试。属于版本同步问题的典型案例，直接影响生产级使用。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: 1.59 breaks CI
source_issues.evidence: 用户仅更新 Docker 镜像 tag 从 v1.58.2-noble 到 v1.59.1-noble，但未同步更新 npm 包版本，导致错误 'Executable doesn't exist at /ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1208/chrome-headless-shell-linux64/chrome-headless-shell'，测试套件无法运行。

signals.topic: page.route() 在 Page Object Model 中不可靠地拦截匹配请求，导致初始化期间请求缺少注入头部
signals.summary: 在 Page Object Model 架构中，将 page.route() 放在基类构造函数中扩展给所有页面时，仅有部分匹配请求被拦截，初始化期间的大多数请求没有包含注入的自定义头部，导致测试依赖的 header 篡改变得不可靠。
aliases: page.route intercepts only subset of matching requests POM
route handler race condition page load
page.route in base class constructor missing requests
signals.review_reason: page.route() 是 Playwright 最核心的请求篡改 API，在 POM 模式下不可靠直接导致测试无法正确执行所需的网络拦截逻辑，属于核心功能失效。issue 提供了 HAR 截图证据，明确了影响范围（初始化期间），且为 v1.59.1 的回归或已知限制，主流程失败明确。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: page.route used in Page Object Model does not reliably intercept all matching requests
source_issues.evidence: 用户使用 POM 基类构造函数注册 page.route()，注入 'x-test-header'，但初始页面加载期间大量请求没有包含该 header，截图和 HAR 导出生动证明了部分请求未被拦截的问题，且无任何警告。

signals.topic: Playwright VSCode 扩展连接 ETIMEDOUT 导致测试列表无法加载（Test Explorer 为空）
signals.summary: 在 Windows 系统上，Playwright VSCode 扩展尝试连接测试列表时出现 'connect ETIMEDOUT ::1:55606' 错误，导致 Test Explorer 视图显示为空，用户无法通过 IDE 运行任何测试。
aliases: playwright vscode extension test explorer empty ETIMEDOUT
vscode extension can't populate test list connection timeout
playwright test discovery fails in vscode windows
signals.review_reason: VSCode 扩展是 Playwright 最主流的 IDE 集成方式，测试列表无法加载直接阻断用户的日常开发工作流。issue 提供了具体错误信息、系统环境（Windows 11, VSCode 1.116.0）和扩展版本，用户明确指出这是最近的回归，关键功能（测试发现）不可用。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: VSCode extension - error connect ETIMEDOUT while populating test list
source_issues.evidence: Windows 用户使用 Playwright VSCode 扩展 1.1.17 时，Test Explorer 空白，报 'connect ETIMEDOUT ::1:55606' 错误，import 语句被标红，用户无法发现和运行任何测试（用户表示'这以前是正常的，几天前开始出问题'）。

signals.topic: WebKit/Linux 下 PerformanceNavigationTiming 的 domInteractive 和 domContentLoadedEventEnd 返回 0（版本 1.59.0 回归）
signals.summary: 从 Playwright 1.59.0 开始，WebKit/Linux 下 PerformanceNavigationTiming API 的 domInteractive 和 domContentLoadedEventEnd 字段始终返回 0，导致依赖这些指标进行性能监控的测试和工具彻底失效。
aliases: webkit linux PerformanceNavigationTiming domInteractive returns 0 regression
domContentLoadedEventEnd zero in WebKit after 1.59 upgrade
signals.review_reason: PerformanceNavigationTiming 是 Web 性能测试的标准 API，返回全 0 直接导致依赖该数据的性能监控工具和基准测试失效。issue 被明确标记为 Regression，有完整的版本对照证据和上游 bug 链接，影响的是性能测量这一关键功能，但 count=1（单 issue），按规则降级为 P1。

source_issues.title: [Regression]: WebKit — PerformanceNavigationTiming.domInteractive and domContentLoadedEventEnd always return 0
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告 WebKit/Linux（1.59.0/1.59.1）下 domInteractive 和 domContentLoadedEventEnd 返回 0，loadEventEnd 正常；提供了详细版本对照表确认回归引入版本（1.59.0-alpha-2026-03-12 对应 WebKit rev 2267），关联上游 WebKit bug #312861，并明确指出这影响了依赖 Navigation Timing Level 2 spec 的性能测试。

signals.topic: Python Redis connector: vector search crashes, delete silently fails, FT.CREATE PREFIX malformed — all core CRUD operations blocked
signals.summary: The Python Redis connector has three critical bugs in the same code path: (1) FT.SEARCH vector search raises AttributeError due to redisvl API incompatibility (>=0.5 required but code uses 0.4 API); (2) RedisJsonCollection.delete() silently fails when prefix_collection_name_to_key_names=True (key not prefixed before JSON.DEL); (3) FT.CREATE sends PREFIX as one character per entry instead of the collection name — all three block core data operations and existing integration tests cover none of these paths.
signals.review_reason: All three bugs are in the same Redis connector code path and collectively block every core CRUD operation (upsert, get, delete, search). Each has concrete wire-level reproduction evidence and is confirmed to have zero test coverage. The silent-failure nature of the delete and PREFIX bugs makes them especially dangerous in multi-collection deployments.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Vector search (FT.SEARCH) via the Python Redis connector is broken
source_issues.evidence: Vector search raises AttributeError: 'StorageType' object has no attribute 'index' on every FT.SEARCH call due to redisvl API break at 0.5.0. redisvl ~0.4 pin resolves to 0.15.0. Confirmed by author with wire-level reproduction.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: RedisJsonCollection.delete() silently fails when prefix_collection_name_to_key_names is enabled
source_issues.evidence: delete() sends JSON.DEL on raw key instead of prefixed key. Record remains after delete with no error raised. Confirmed via redis-cli MONITOR showing JSON.DEL without prefix. Hashset sibling correctly prefixes keys.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Redis connector sends malformed FT.CREATE PREFIX (one prefix per character of collection name)
source_issues.evidence: redis-py treats string prefix as iterable of characters. In multi-collection Redis deployments this causes index overlap across collections, silently corrupting data routing.

signals.topic: Google/Vertex AI Gemini connector: multiple function/tool calls fail with 400 'number of function response parts' API error — blocks multi-tool agent workflows
signals.summary: When Gemini model makes multiple function calls in a single response, the SK connector sends function responses as multiple separate role=function messages (one per function) instead of bundling them into a single role=function message with all responses in one parts array. Gemini API returns 400 'Please ensure the number of function response parts equals the number of function call parts'. This breaks any agent that needs more than one tool per turn.
signals.review_reason: This blocks any real-world multi-tool agent workflow with Gemini. Every agent that needs more than one tool per turn gets a hard 400 API error and fails completely. The wire-level evidence shows the exact malformed request structure, making this a clear, high-impact regression.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Gemini - 2 parallel plugin call exception: number of function response parts is equal to the number of function call parts of the function call turn
source_issues.evidence: Active open issue. When 2 tools are called by Gemini 2.0-flash, the next request fails with 400 and message 'number of function response parts equals number of function call parts'. Request shows 2 separate role=function messages instead of 1 with 2 parts. Confirmed by wire-level request/response comparison.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: VertexAIGeminiChatCompletion 400 bad request when model makes multiple function calls in one message
source_issues.evidence: Same 400 error reproduced with VertexAIGeminiChatCompletion using gemini-2.5-flash. Root cause identical: function responses split across multiple role=function messages instead of bundled in one.

signals.topic: GoogleAIGeminiChatCompletion: tools/functions field not included in API request — function calling entirely non-functional (closed stale)
signals.summary: GoogleAIGeminiChatCompletion connector does not include the tools field in the API request to Gemini, making function calling completely non-operational regardless of plugin registration. Users who set up function calling with Gemini get zero function calls back with no indication of why. The issue was closed as stale without a fix being merged.
signals.review_reason: Although closed as stale, this represents complete function-calling failure for Google AI Gemini users. Users who follow standard SK patterns get zero function calls with no error message, making debugging nearly impossible. The root cause (settings not serialized into API request) is well-evidenced with trace logs.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: GoogleAIGeminiChatCompletion doesn't send tools/functions in API request
source_issues.evidence: Closed as stale. Trace log shows function_choice_behavior settings are recognized but 'ToolCallBehavior' is null and the tools field is absent from the serialized JSON request. Function calls never fire despite correct plugin registration.

signals.topic: ExtensionData parameters in OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings not forwarded to HTTP JSON payload (closed stale)
signals.summary: ExtensionData dictionary set on OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings (used for provider-specific parameters like enable_thinking) is not included in the HTTP JSON request body. Users trying to use custom provider parameters get no effect with no error message. The issue was closed as stale without a fix.
signals.review_reason: Blocks use of provider-specific parameters (e.g. enable_thinking, ReasoningBudget) that require custom fields in the request body. While not a main-flow blocker for basic usage, it prevents users from controlling advanced model features, which is a real workflow limitation.

source_issues.title: Bug: ExtensionData parameters not included in HTTP JSON request when using OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings
source_issues.evidence: Closed as stale. User provided exact code showing ExtensionData with enable_thinking=false not appearing in generated JSON payload. No error raised — parameters silently dropped.

signals.topic: Windows sandbox cannot spawn shell processes (CreateProcessAsUserW error 5) blocking git/gh usage after v0.124.0 update
signals.summary: After upgrading to v0.124.0, Windows users cannot use git/gh commands because the sandbox fails to spawn shell processes with CreateProcessAsUserW error code 5 (Access Denied). Even with Full Access permissions, sandboxed commands fail and escalation is also broken on Windows.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断: Windows用户升级到v0.124.0后完全无法使用git/gh命令,这是开发工作流的核心操作。即使授予Full Access权限也无法解决,且escalation机制本身在Windows上也失效,导致用户核心开发工具完全不可用。

source_issues.title: Windows sandbox cannot spawn shell processes after escalation disabled
source_issues.evidence: Normal sandboxed shell commands failed with CreateProcessAsUserW failed: 5. Escalated shell commands worked initially, then escalation itself became unavailable. rg -n and bash -lc commands both fail.

source_issues.title: fatal: Unable to create '.git/index.lock': Permission denied, has full permissions
source_issues.evidence: Codex is completely unable to use gh or git. Default permissions: non-permission commands fail. Full permissions: virtually nothing works. Git commands fail with permission errors even with Full Access granted.

signals.topic: 1M context window silently ignored after GPT-5.5 upgrade — config settings not respected
signals.summary: After GPT-5.5 release, users who had working 1M context window with GPT-5.4 find it gone. The model_context_window and model_auto_compact_token_limit config settings are silently ignored or silently reduced (e.g. 1M → 258k). No error or warning is shown.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能降级: 1M上下文窗口是GPT-5.5的关键卖点,但用户在升级后发现该功能实际不可用(被静默降级到258k)。这直接损害了用户对付费升级的预期,且配置被静默忽略没有任何提示,影响依赖大上下文的专业用户工作流。count=2且明确样例链接,符合P0条件。

source_issues.title: 1m context window gone after Gpt 5.5 Release
source_issues.evidence: User had 1M context window working with GPT-5.4 via config.toml. After GPT-5.5 announcement claiming 1M support, the feature is gone from the Codex app. Config still shows model_context_window = 1000000 but effective context is reduced.

source_issues.title: config.toml context window settings are not respected
source_issues.evidence: model_context_window and model_auto_compact_token_limit settings silently ignored. Setting 1M results in ~258k used without any validation error or warning. User cannot control context behavior through config. Impact: users cannot reliably control context behavior.

signals.topic: Model selector does not persist on new chat — user-selected model reverts to default
signals.summary: When starting a new chat, the model selector does not persist the user's selection — it reverts to the default model (e.g. GPT-5.4 instead of selected GPT-5.5). Also GPT-5.5 selected in composer at start does not persist and switches back to 5.4.
aliases: Model selection not persisted in new chat
GPT-5.5 selector reverts to GPT-5.4 on new chat
signals.review_reason: 体验下降: 用户每次新建聊天时模型选择无法保持,需要反复手动重新选择。虽然不影响核心功能可用性,但影响效率且用户需要频繁重复操作,count=2有视频证据支撑,定位P2边缘痛点。

source_issues.title: Model selector broken on new chat
source_issues.evidence: Cannot change model or reasoning for a new chat (project chat or new chat feature). Selector does not change — selection is not applied.

source_issues.title: selecting 5.5 in composer from start does not persist
source_issues.evidence: When selecting GPT-5.5 from the composer in a start chat it does not persist and switches back to GPT-5.4. Video evidence provided.

signals.topic: Subagent lifecycle leak causes session freeze and blocks parallel multi-agent workflows
signals.summary: Codex leaks orphaned subagents that remain after work is complete. These invisible subagents continue counting against the launch limit, causing 'too many subagents launched' errors and eventual hard-freeze of the entire session, even with RAM/swap available. Manual cleanup from main thread only partially works.
signals.review_reason: 严重工作流阻断: 对于使用多Agent并行分解任务的用户,subagent泄漏导致整个会话最终冻结并需要手动kill。这不是边缘问题而是核心并行工作流的完全阻断,且没有用户可见的生命周期控制来恢复。Freeze发生在有足够RAM的情况下,表明是进程管理问题而非资源耗尽。

source_issues.title: Persistent orphaned subagents, missing lifecycle controls, and eventual session freezes
source_issues.evidence: Subagents remain stuck after work is finished, Codex reaches its own subagent limit, automatic cleanup removes only 1-3 subagents leaving orphaned ones still counted. Main thread cleanup produces the same partial result. Hard freeze occurs with free RAM available. No user-facing lifecycle controls exist. Blocks all subagent-heavy parallel workflows.

signals.topic: Codex review tool fails in sandboxed environments (bwrap/user-namespace) and does not request escalation — blocks local pre-push code review
signals.summary: In Replit/workspace-style environments where sandboxed commands fail with bwrap namespace errors, the code review tool cannot inspect local commits and does not fall back to escalation or provide actionable feedback. Local pre-push code review is completely unavailable.
aliases: local commit review blocked by sandbox
signals.review_reason: 工作流阻断: 在Replit等沙箱受限环境中,本地pre-push代码审查功能完全不可用。虽然这是单条issue,但明确的主流程阻断(核心代码审查功能)+强用户影响证据(审查工具无法提供任何可操作结果),且回归了之前版本可用的功能,应保留为P1。

source_issues.title: Codex review tool cannot inspect local commits due to bwrap sandbox error and does not request escalation
source_issues.evidence: Review tool attempts sandboxed local commands only, fails on bwrap, and does not request escalation. Commits were local-only so GitHub fallback couldn't find SHAs. Local pre-push code review is unavailable in this environment. Normal Codex commands in the same session work when rerun with escalation. This workflow worked with GPT-5.4.

signals.topic: Windows platform compatibility: sandbox module import fails and Modal local sandboxes do not work
signals.summary: On Windows, importing `agents.sandbox.sandboxes` immediately raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'` because the package eagerly imports Unix-only backends. Additionally, Modal sandbox with `remote=False` fails with `WorkspaceStartError` (executable not found in PATH), and skill source directories with `PurePosixPath` semantics fail with `SkillsConfigError`. These three separate issues share the root cause of Windows path and platform assumptions, collectively making the sandbox subsystem unusable on Windows.
signals.review_reason: Three confirmed Windows-specific bugs in the sandbox subsystem, all with reproducible repro steps. Count=3 meets the threshold. While Windows may not be the primary target platform, the sandbox import crash (fcntl) completely prevents the module from being loaded on Windows, which is a hard blocker for that platform. Not P0 because it is platform-scoped (Linux is unaffected) and the primary SDK agent workflows do not require sandboxes.

source_issues.title: Windows: import agents.sandbox.sandboxes fails with ModuleNotFoundError: fcntl
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug with repro steps: `python -c "import agents.sandbox.sandboxes"` fails immediately with `ModuleNotFoundError: fcntl` on Windows. The Unix-only backend from `unix_local.py` is imported eagerly in `__init__.py`.

source_issues.title: `WorkspaceStartError` on Windows
source_issues.evidence: Modal sandbox with `remote=False` on Windows raises `WorkspaceStartError: failed to start session`. The `resolve-workspace-path` executable is not found in PATH on Windows. Same user filing both Windows sandbox issues.

source_issues.title: Skill source directory unavailable on Windows
source_issues.evidence: `skills_source_path` resolves to `\skills` on Windows (backslash) vs `/skills` on Linux (forward slash), causing `SkillsConfigError: lazy skill source directory is unavailable`. Setting `PurePosixPath` raises a Pydantic validation error instead.

signals.topic: HITL resume after rejection drops tool output for successfully executed non-approval tools, causing API 400 error
signals.summary: When a model issues parallel tool calls where some require approval and some do not, resuming after rejecting the approval-gated calls fails with `BadRequestError: No tool output found for function call <call_id>`. The SDK incorrectly marks the successfully-executed non-approval tool's output as 'already sent to server', causing `prepare_input()` to drop it. The API then sees a dangling function_call with no output.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed workflow failure with deterministic reproduction. The issue is a logical bug in conversation state tracking that causes a 400 API error during the HITL resume path. While count=1, the severity is high (main workflow blocked) and the repro is explicit and complete. Not P0 because the HITL parallel-approval pattern is a specific edge case, not the most common main path.

source_issues.title: HITL resume drops tool output when parallel calls mix approval-gated and non-approval tools
source_issues.evidence: Bug is deterministic (runs in <1 second, no API needed). Repro code shows `hydrate_from_state()` unconditionally adds `call_id` to `server_tool_call_ids` for locally-generated outputs that were never sent to the API, causing `prepare_input()` to skip them on resume. The API then returns 400 'No tool output found for function call call_DIAG.' The user provides both a deterministic test and a live-API variant.

signals.topic: Realtime Tools race condition: tool-triggered create.response causes RealtimeError when a response is already in progress
signals.summary: When a RealtimeAgent tool executes while a response is already in progress, the tool's execution triggers a 'create.response' event that raises `RealtimeError: Conversation already has an active response in progress`. This causes the agent to get stuck waiting for customer input, blocking the realtime conversation flow.
signals.review_reason: The realtime tool call path causes an explicit `RealtimeError` that blocks the main realtime conversation flow. The agent gets stuck waiting for customer input, which is a clear user experience degradation in a realtime use case. While count=1, the production severity (v0.14.2 still affected with 4 comments from users) and the explicit error message provide strong evidence. Not P0 because the realtime feature is an optional extension, not the core agent execution path.

source_issues.title: Realtime Tools cause agent response to cut off
source_issues.evidence: Explicit error: `RealtimeError(message='Conversation already has an active response in progress: resp_DUvxzRrEe3YZSdwIqBdVn. Wait until the response is finished before creating a new one.')`. The agent gets stuck and waits for customer request. Affects async tool calls and cases where 'create.response' is triggered outside the agent while the agent runs tools. 4 comments confirm engagement from community members. Version v0.14.2 in production still affected.

signals.topic: RealtimeSession does not emit history_updated event for transcript_delta, breaking UI state sync
signals.summary: RealtimeSession updates its local `_history` when receiving a `transcript_delta` event, but does not emit a `history_updated` event. UIs following the official realtime docs (which recommend using history_added/history_updated for UI state) will not see live transcript changes even though the session history has already changed internally.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed API inconsistency: the realtime session updates internal state without emitting the documented high-level event, causing UIs that follow the official docs to miss live transcript updates. Count=1 and the impact is UX-level (missing events, not crash or block), so P2 is appropriate. The issue is actionable with a clear fix.

source_issues.title: RealtimeSession does not emit `history_updated` for `transcript_delta`
source_issues.evidence: Bug confirmed via minimal repro code. `session._history` is updated by `transcript_delta` but only the raw model event is emitted to the queue, not a `history_updated` event. The realtime docs explicitly state that `history_added`/`history_updated` are the main events for UI state. 2 comments indicate community interest.

signals.topic: transform_string_function_style silently renames tool names with spaces without emitting a warning
signals.summary: The function `transform_string_function_style` replaces spaces with underscores before comparing the input to decide whether to emit a warning. This means tool names like 'My Tool' are silently transformed to 'my_tool' with no log output, making it hard to debug name mismatches between the tool definition and tool calls that reference the original name.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed code bug with clear reproduction and fix. The impact is that tool names with spaces are silently transformed without any log, potentially causing mismatches between tool definitions and callers. While not a hard blocker, it causes silent data corruption (tool name change) that is hard to debug. Count=1 with subtle UX impact, so P2 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: fix: transform_string_function_style silently transforms space-containing names without warning
source_issues.evidence: Bug is confirmed in code: the function does `name = name.replace(' ', '_')` then checks `if transformed_name != name` against the already-modified name, so the warning never fires for space-only transformations. The user provides a specific fix (preserve original_name before modification).

signals.topic: Responses API output_text null text field crashes SDK parsing and property access
signals.summary: 当 Responses API 返回 text: null 的 output_text 条目时，SDK 的 Response.output_text 属性和 responses.parse() 均抛出异常，导致数据无法访问。
signals.review_reason: 两个独立用户在不同日期（3月25日和4月6日）报告了完全相同的根因：API 返回的 output_text.text=null 导致 SDK 侧 TypeError。这不是边缘案例——Responses API 正常工作流被直接阻断，用户无法读取任何包含 null output_text 的响应内容，属于主流程失败。

source_issues.title: Response.output_text and responses.parse fail when an output_text item has text: null
source_issues.evidence: strict response parsing rejects ResponseOutputText.text=null; parsed responses attempt structured parsing on null text and raise TypeError; #3062 related PR exists confirming the bug surface

source_issues.title: Response.output_text fails to handle null text values in content items
source_issues.evidence: Response.output_text property raises TypeError when concatenating None values; occurs on gpt-oss-safeguard-120b model and other models that return null text; code-level root cause identified in output_text property implementation

signals.topic: vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll() 在文件卡在 in_progress 状态时无限挂起
signals.summary: 上传文件到 vector store 后，upload_and_poll() 在文件状态永远卡在 in_progress 时会无限等待，没有超时机制，导致进程挂死。
signals.review_reason: upload_and_poll() 无超时机制是明确的 API 端挂起 bug——当 vector store 文件处理卡住时（status=in_progress 永久不变，last_error=null），SDK 侧没有任何保护，用户进程会无限等待。这直接阻断依赖文件上传完成后的后续工作流，属于主流程阻断级 bug。

source_issues.title: vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll() can hang indefinitely with file status stuck at in_progress
source_issues.evidence: upload_and_poll() never returns when file stuck at status=in_progress forever; last_error stays null; raw uploaded file already status=processed; hang is in vector store file processing/indexing layer; confirmed with openai==2.31.0 Python 3.12 on April 15-16 2026

signals.topic: GPT-5.4-mini 搭配图片/文件输入时 500 错误率高达 95%，同参数下 GPT-5.4 正常
signals.summary: 使用 ResponsesInputImageParam 携带图片 URL 请求 gpt-5.4-mini 模型时，API 端重试 3 次均返回 500 错误，但同参数下 gpt-5.4 工作正常。
aliases: image input only affects mini model
signals.review_reason: GPT-5.4-mini 在携带图片参数时 API 端返回 500 导致 SDK 重试失败，是明确的主流程失败场景。用户被迫在 gpt-5.4-mini（更小更便宜）和图片输入功能之间二选一，在生产环境中直接造成功能不可用和成本损失（重试浪费 quota）。

source_issues.title: GPT-5.4-Mini returns 500 internal errors 95% of the time when providing input files / images as parameters
source_issues.evidence: gpt-5.4-mini with ResponseInputImageParam throws retry 3 times with 500 internal error; exact same input with gpt-5.4 works fine; reproducible by sending request with ResponseInputImageParam with valid URL

signals.topic: AsyncResponses 客户端使用 structured outputs 时存在内存泄漏（Pydantic schema 无限重建）
signals.summary: 使用 AsyncResponses 客户端的 parse_response 解析 structured outputs 时，TextFormatT TypeVar 导致 Pydantic schema 无限重建，内存持续增长。
signals.review_reason: 内存泄漏会在长期运行的异步服务中持续消耗内存直至 OOM，显著影响服务稳定性。用户反复调用 structured outputs 解析时每次都会累积泄漏，是明显的关键功能损害。虽然 count=1，但有详细的火焰图证据和精确的根因定位，内存泄漏属于高严重性体验下降。

source_issues.title: Async Responses Structured Outputs Memory leak
source_issues.evidence: Flame graph shows unbounded pydantic schema rebuilds in parse_response; construct_type_unchecked called with TypeVar-subscripted generics (ParsedResponseOutputText[TextFormatT], etc.); TextFormatT is free module-level TypeVar causing schema rebuild on each call; confirmed with openai==2.31.0 pydantic>=2 Python 3.13

signals.topic: Responses API 中 tool-call-only turns 不触发 context compaction，导致 agent 循环中上下文无限增长
signals.summary: 当 Responses API 仅返回 function_call 输出时（不含 message），不会发出 compaction 事件，导致多轮 tool-call 场景中上下文不断增长直至超出限制。
aliases: compaction not emitted on tool calls
context grows without compaction in tool loops
signals.review_reason: 在 agent 工具调用循环中，上下文 compaction 不触发会导致对话历史无限增长，最终触发 token 限制错误。这是 SDK 的服务端 compaction 逻辑与 tool-call 输出类型的组合 bug，直接破坏依赖上下文压缩的 agent 工作流，属于主流程失败。

source_issues.title: Bug: server-side compaction is not emitted on Responses tool-call-only turns
source_issues.evidence: With context_management=[{type: compaction, compact_threshold: 1000}] and store=False, tool-call-only turns produce no compaction item; compaction only appears when assistant message is returned; agent loops with consecutive tool-call turns have unbounded context growth; openai-python SDK issue confirmed

signals.topic: Persistent ACP sessions re-spawn adapter process on every turn instead of reusing pooled client
signals.summary: Persistent ACP sessions pay a full cold-start cost on every `sessions_send` because `runTurn` unconditionally calls `client.close()` in the `finally` block without a symmetric "return to pool" path. The adapter process is torn down after every turn, defeating `acp.runtime.ttlMinutes` and the session pool. Measured cold-start penalty: ~23s for Claude, 74-112s for Gemini per turn. Users must wait for full re-spawn on every multi-turn interaction.
aliases: adapter process not retained across turns
persistent client lost after runTurn finally
signals.review_reason: This is a main-workflow-blocking bug. Every multi-turn persistent session pays a full cold-start penalty on every turn because the pooled client is unconditionally closed. Measured latency impact is 23-112s per turn, which is a significant cost and UX degradation for the core ACP session workflow.

source_issues.title: [bug] persistent ACP client not returned to pool after runTurn
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows adapter child process (PID 104981) exits after turn 1, re-spawns for turn 2 with new timestamp and PID. Local validation confirms fix retains same PID across turns. Cold-start latency 23s (Claude) / 74-112s (Gemini) per blocked turn.

signals.topic: Creating a new codex session via acpx does not register the session in codex's own session list, preventing session resumption
signals.summary: When creating a new codex session via `acpx codex sessions new`, the session is not registered in codex's own session store. Running `codex resume <session-id>` fails with 'No saved session found'. The same workflow works correctly for `kimi`. Users cannot resume codex sessions created through acpx.
aliases: codex session not persisted after acpx creation
codex resume fails for acpx-created sessions
signals.review_reason: Session persistence is a key advertised feature of acpx. When session resumption fails for codex but works for kimi, it is a clear regression that blocks the user's ability to continue work across sessions. The user impact is unambiguous — the session cannot be resumed at all.

source_issues.title: new codex session 后，并没有注册到 codex 的 session，kimi 是没问题的
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction steps show `acpx codex sessions new` succeeds and returns session ID, but `codex resume <session-id>` immediately fails with 'No saved session found'. Same workflow with `kimi` agent works correctly — `kimi --resume` successfully resumes the session.

signals.topic: Security scanner false positives block legitimate skills from being installed
signals.summary: VirusTotal Code Insight and ClawHub security scanners are incorrectly flagging legitimate skills as suspicious/malicious, causing installation failures in both interactive and non-interactive (CI/CD, Docker, MCP server) environments. Multiple publishers across diverse domains (trading SDKs, IM plugins, productivity tools, cultural/educational skills) are affected.
aliases: VT Code Insight false positive blocks
signals.review_reason: 11 distinct GitHub issue reports from independent publishers across diverse domains (trading SDKs, enterprise IM, productivity tools, cultural skills) all reporting the same root cause: ClawHub security scanners (VirusTotal Code Insight, LLM moderation) incorrectly flag legitimate skills as suspicious/malicious. The user impact is severe: in non-interactive environments (CI/CD pipelines, Docker builds, MCP server bootstraps), affected skills hard-fail on 'clawhub install' with no way to proceed silently. The adlai88 case (#1787) provides concrete evidence of 14 blocked skills with 8.3k downloads, explicit CI/CD blocking, and direct revenue/signal loss. This is a systemic scanner quality problem affecting publishers across the entire platform, not isolated incidents.

signals.topic: CLI publish flow undocumented; required manifest fields only surface on failed publish, causing forced version bumps
signals.summary: The 'npx clawhub package publish' CLI command is completely undocumented on ClawHub docs and web UI. When publishing a code-plugin, two required package.json fields (openclaw.compat.pluginApi and openclaw.build.openclawVersion) are not documented anywhere and only surface as Convex errors at publish time. ClawHub version-locks every failed attempt, so each missing-field discovery costs a patch version bump permanently.
signals.review_reason: Single issue but with extremely explicit, reproducible user impact: every code-plugin publisher who discovers the CLI independently must burn multiple patch version bumps just to find the required manifest fields. The version-locking behavior means no recovery is possible — phantom failed versions are permanently committed to npm registry. This directly blocks the code-plugin publish workflow for any publisher who doesn't already know the undocumented fields. The absence of preflight validation means users cannot discover what they are missing before committing a version slot.

source_issues.title: docs: CLI publish flow undocumented; required openclaw.compat.pluginApi + openclaw.build.openclawVersion fields only surface on failed publish
source_issues.evidence: Full reproduction steps provided: fresh package publish fails twice with cryptic Convex errors for two separate missing fields, each failure version-locks the bump. Author lost 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 on n8n-ops-mcp before finding the required-field set buried in /usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw/docs/snippets/. Canonical template only exists in an npm-installed file, not in any public docs. No preflight validation; no way to unpublish phantom failed versions.

signals.topic: Early failed/flagged skill versions permanently poison all subsequent versions on ClawHub, even after fixes
signals.summary: When a skill has early versions with security flags or failures, ClawHub permanently marks the entire skill as bad and displays suspicious/failed status on all versions, including current clean versions. Users viewing the skill page see the failed status even when the latest version is verified clean, causing distrust and preventing adoption.
aliases: historical security flags poison skill reputation
old version flags persist on new versions
signals.review_reason: Author describes a critical administrative skill (emergency rollback for remote OpenClaw admins) that is now permanently distrusted on ClawHub due to historical artifact flags on old versions, even though the latest version is verified clean. This is not merely a cosmetic issue — users encountering the skill page see a failed/suspicious badge that undermines trust in a security-critical tool. No mechanism exists to unpublish or suppress old artifact versions that are poisoning the skill's reputation.

source_issues.title: early versions with issues cause all subsequent versions to show failed even when they show clean
source_issues.evidence: Author's skill is confirmed clean in current version but ClawHub 'permanently marked it bad' due to earlier releases; suspicious status shown on the skill page even though clicking through shows the latest artifact is clean. Author states: 'this is a critical skill for any remote openclaw admin' but the old artifacts 'poisoning the new' makes it hard to demonstrate trustworthiness. No way to unpublish or hide the old failed versions.

signals.topic: 认证失败时的重试循环无退避策略，导致网关被触发限速，使用户无法连接
signals.summary: 当认证失败（token 不匹配、签名无效或触发限速）时，OpenClaw 节点客户端每 1 秒重试一次且不退避，导致：1) 向网关发送大量失败认证请求；2) 触发网关 rate limiter；3) 每次重试重置限速冷却时间，使问题恶化；4) 每分钟在日志中产生数百条相同错误。最终导致用户的主流程（与网关建立连接）被完全阻断。
aliases: rate limiter triggered by auth failures
signals.review_reason: 认证失败重试循环导致主流程（节点连接网关）完全阻断，且存在具体日志证据（每秒数百条相同错误），触发网关限速机制使问题自我恶化。这是明确的会话状态问题，导致用户必须手动干预才能恢复连接。

source_issues.title: bug: aggressive retry loop on authentication failures triggers gateway rate limiter
source_issues.evidence: 日志显示每约1秒产生一条 'unauthorized: gateway token mismatch' 错误，持续不断；随后触发 'too many failed authentication attempts' 限速；重试计数器在每次循环时重置为1，导致指数退避(1s→2s→4s→...)永远无法触发。

signals.topic: Claude CLI backend session scaffolding exceeds context window — sub-Opus models silently fail to run on heavy workspaces
signals.summary: The claude-cli provider backend builds a pre-turn harness (CLAUDE.md, hooks, plugin sync, auto-memory) that exceeds the context window of claude-sonnet-4-6 (195k) and claude-haiku-4-5 (200k), causing silent FailoverError on every turn and forcing fallback to different models.
aliases: sub-opus models unusable on heavy workspaces
Prompt too long FailoverError for sonnet/haiku
signals.review_reason: Three issues confirm that the claude-cli backend session scaffold exceeds the context window of sub-Opus models, causing silent FailoverError on every prompt. Users paying for a Claude Code subscription cannot use sonnet/haiku on typical workstations. This is a functional blocker for the claude-cli provider with clear user impact evidence (concrete error messages, affected model IDs, user workflow described).

source_issues.title: Feature: slim mode to pass --bare to claude-cli backend (unlock sub-opus models on heavy workspaces)
source_issues.evidence: On heavy workspace, claude-sonnet-4-6 fails with FailoverError: Prompt is too long. claude-haiku-4-5 same error. claude-opus-4-7 (1024k ctx) works. Sub-opus models are effectively unusable — requests silently fail over to fallback.

source_issues.title: Feature request: slim/bare mode for claude-cli backend to support sub-opus models
source_issues.evidence: Feature request citing that the claude-cli backend session scaffold exceeds 200k tokens, making sub-Opus models unusable.

source_issues.title: Feature request: slim-mode / pass --bare to claude-cli backend so sub-Opus Claude models fit the context window
source_issues.evidence: Explicitly states every Claude model with <200k context (claude-sonnet-4-6 at 195k, claude-haiku-4-5 at 200k) is unusable — requests silently fail with FailoverError.

signals.topic: Plugin runtime dependency fails to resolve after update — Discord provider crash-loops, Telegram channel fails to load
signals.summary: After upgrading to 4.21+/4.22, the plugin-runtime-deps cache embeds a stale versioned hash that cannot resolve 'openclaw', causing Discord to crash-loop on startup and Telegram channel to fail loading.
aliases: plugin runtime deps cache stale hash
Cannot find package openclaw from plugin-runtime-deps
Telegram plugin fails to load after update
signals.review_reason: Two distinct channels (Discord and Telegram) both break with the same root cause after the 4.22 update. The plugin-runtime-deps cache embeds a stale versioned hash causing ESM subpath imports to fail, crash-looping Discord entirely and preventing Telegram from loading. This blocks entire channel integrations and is a multi-channel regression.

source_issues.title: 4.22: Discord provider crash-loops with 'Cannot find package openclaw' on npm global install (ESM subpath import fails from plugin-runtime-deps cache)
source_issues.evidence: On clean npm install -g openclaw@2026.4.22, every Discord provider instance crash-loops immediately after plugin provisioning with: Cannot find package 'openclaw' imported from .../.openclaw/plugin-runtime-deps/openclaw-2026.4.22-4eca502.

signals.topic: Web UI chat messages disappear immediately — scope upgrade approval loop permanently blocks user replies
signals.summary: The Control UI chat sends messages but they vanish instantly because a continuous scope-upgrade approval loop never resolves, preventing any reply from being sent.
aliases: scope upgrade loop blocks chat replies
signals.review_reason: A behavior bug that blocks the core chat interaction in the Control UI. The scope upgrade loop causes message loss and prevents user replies entirely, representing a significant degradation of the primary user-facing interface.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Web UI chat messages disappear immediately - scope upgrade approval loop blocks replies
source_issues.evidence: Bug report: sending a message in the Control UI chat causes the message bubble to disappear immediately with no reply, due to a continuous scope upgrade approval loop that persists even after approving.

signals.topic: 256KB hardcoded stdout buffer limit aborts long claude-cli turns — triggers silent model fallback during extended thinking
signals.summary: The claude-cli runtime hardcodes a 256KB stdout buffer limit. When Claude CLI emits a stream-json line larger than this (common with extended thinking on Opus 4.7), the live session is aborted and falls back to the next configured model. Observed 8 times in one day.
signals.review_reason: The hardcoded 256KB buffer limit actively causes live session aborts during extended thinking operations. Each abort silently falls back to a different model, causing inconsistent user experience and unexpected model switches. With 8 aborts recorded in one day this is not edge-case — it is a recurring failure pattern that disrupts the primary workflow.

source_issues.title: Make CLAUDE_LIVE_MAX_STDOUT_BUFFER_CHARS configurable (256KB hardcoded limit aborts long claude-cli turns)
source_issues.evidence: 8 overflow aborts in a single day on one host, all on claude-opus-4-7. Every abort triggered a fallback to gpt-5.5 or grok-4, causing inconsistent model/voice and perceived timeouts. Body: 'Claude CLI stdout buffer exceeded limit' causes model fallback decision.

signals.topic: Bundled HTTP MCP client times out against hosted SSE server after 4.22 upgrade — all HTTP MCP servers fail to start
signals.summary: After upgrading from 4.12 to 4.22, all HTTP-transport MCP servers fail to start at gateway boot with 15-30s SSE/stream timeout. The same endpoint responds correctly to direct curl in ~450ms, and Claude Code's own MCP client connects fine, isolating the bug to OpenClaw's bundled HTTP/2 SSE transport.
signals.review_reason: This regression in 4.22 breaks all HTTP-transport MCP server integrations. The bundled MCP client times out while the endpoint is healthy (verified by curl) and Claude Code's own MCP client works, isolating this to OpenClaw's bundled transport. Users who rely on external MCP servers lose all MCP functionality at gateway boot.

source_issues.title: Bundled HTTP MCP client times out against hosted SSE server even when endpoint responds in <1s
source_issues.evidence: After upgrading from 2026.4.12 to 2026.4.22, all HTTP-transport MCP servers fail to start at gateway boot with 15-30s SSE/stream timeout. Direct curl to same URL returns HTTP 200 in ~450ms. Claude Code MCP client connects fine. Bug isolated to OpenClaw's bundled HTTP/2 SSE transport.

signals.topic: WhatsApp Dispatch 连接成功但无法处理/响应消息
signals.summary: 用户将 WhatsApp 通过 Dispatch 连接后，状态显示已连接（绿点），但消息无法被检测、处理或回复。手机上消息显示已读（蓝勾），但桌面应用主控制台无任何响应，主流程完全阻断。
signals.review_reason: WhatsApp Dispatch 是用户核心使用场景之一。该功能显示连接成功但实际完全无法处理消息，属于主流程阻断性 bug。用户明确可见：连接绿点正常但消息石沉大海，蓝勾确认消息被读取但无任何应用响应。不同于一般性功能异常，此场景下手势应用完全不可用，是明确的用户体验痛点。

source_issues.title: WhatsApp Dispatch connected but not processing or sending messages windows
source_issues.evidence: WhatsApp 状态显示 Connected（绿点），用户发送消息后手机上显示已读（双蓝勾），但应用主控台保持空闲状态，无任何处理动作。bridge between WhatsApp Web instance and interpreter core is broken. 核心功能在连接显示正常的情况下完全不可用。
