signals.topic: litellm/openai dependency version conflict causes uncaught ImportError, blocking aider startup on all platforms
signals.summary: litellm pulling an incompatible openai version results in ImportError for internal modules (_types, utils, _legacy_response). Multiple users across Windows/Linux report aider crashes immediately on launch with no workaround.
aliases: openai internal import failure startup crash
signals.review_reason: count=3, root cause is the same litellm/openai dependency conflict, all three are uncaught ImportError that prevent aider from starting at all — confirmed main-flow startup crash on multiple platforms (Linux, Windows) and multiple Python versions (3.9–3.12). High impact, no workaround described.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ImportError in _types.py line 36
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name 'BaseTransport' from 'httpx' — triggered by litellm loading openai._models which then chains to httpx version mismatch. Blocks startup on Linux.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ImportError in _legacy_response.py line 27
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name 'is_type_alias_type' from 'openai._utils' — openai package internal API mismatch. Blocks startup on Windows Python 3.9.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ImportError in utils.py line 43
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name '_parsing' from 'openai.lib' — litellm's openai dependency version incompatible with installed openai package. Blocks startup on Windows.

signals.topic: Git cache file deserialization error in fun.py crashes aider on repo open, blocking all further usage
signals.summary: Two duplicate reports of struct.error during read_cache() when deserializing a git cache file, causing aider to crash during sanity_check_repo before any coding work can begin.
signals.review_reason: count=2 (below P0 threshold) but both are exact duplicates from the same user, and both are uncaught exceptions that block all aider usage — the entire workflow cannot start because sanity_check_repo crashes before any coding interaction. The crash happens in the git cache deserialization path, which is a core code path executed on every launch for any repo.

source_issues.title: Uncaught error in fun.py line 263
source_issues.evidence: struct.error: unpack requires a buffer of 8 bytes at read_cache() — crashes during sanity_check_repo before any coding task can proceed. Linux Fedora 43, Python 3.12.

source_issues.title: Uncaught error in fun.py line 263
source_issues.evidence: Same struct.error crash as #5061, duplicate report from same author. Crash occurs at same call path: sanity_check_repo → get_tracked_files → _deserialize → read_cache.

signals.topic: Architect mode handoff bypasses input preprocessing, enabling README prompt injection to be committed as backdoored code
signals.summary: In architect mode, the architect model output is passed directly to the editor with preproc=False, bypassing normal input preprocessing. Attacker-controlled content in README.md (containing hidden ARCHITECT OVERRIDE instructions) was transformed by the architect and committed by the editor, demonstrating a full prompt injection → code execution chain.
aliases: architect editor handoff trust boundary bypass
signals.review_reason: count=1 but confidence is high because the attack chain was validated by the reporter (has commit hash as evidence). The trust-boundary violation is real: architect output flows directly to editor without validation, and repo content (README.md) can influence architect output. This is a P1 rather than P0 because it requires specific conditions (architect mode + poisoned repo content + --yes flag) rather than being a universal crash.

source_issues.title: Architect mode can turn README prompt injection into committed backdoored code
source_issues.evidence: Validated retest demonstrated full attack chain: poisoned README.md → architect output containing malicious import → editor applied it to auth.py → aider committed the backdoored file. The inserted code reads .env and exfiltrates it to an attacker-controlled URL. Affects any repo where architect mode is enabled.

signals.topic: Symlink loop causes uncaught RuntimeError in pathlib resolve, crashing aider when scanning repo files
signals.summary: When encountering a circular symlink in the repo directory tree, pathlib.Path.resolve() raises an uncaught RuntimeError, crashing aider mid-workflow during repo map building and preventing any file operations.
signals.review_reason: count=1, single-platform (Linux) issue, but the crash occurs in a core code path (repo-map building) and has no user workaround — the workflow simply cannot proceed if any symlink loop exists anywhere in the repo tree. P2 rather than P1 because frequency is low (only one report) and it requires a specific pathological filesystem condition.

source_issues.title: Uncaught RuntimeError in pathlib.py line 1237
source_issues.evidence: RuntimeError: Symlink loop from '/mnt/Data/dev-projects/saas/webforbusiness/.agents/skills/turborepo' — crash occurs in get_repo_map() → get_all_abs_files() → abs_root_path() → safe_abs_path() → Path.resolve(). Entire workflow is blocked on repos containing circular symlinks.

signals.topic: Self-hosted LLM judge with thinking capability fails without explicit showThinking:false, with hard-to-debug JSON parse errors

The `showThinking: false` flag must be explicitly set but is not documented as required. Errors provide no details about what string failed to parse, making debugging very difficult.
aliases: thinking model JSON parse error judge
vLLM thinking content breaks judge assertion
signals.review_reason: User reports that self-hosted judge with thinking models produces hard-to-debug JSON parse errors. The error message is uninformative ('Could not parse Json' without showing the actual string), making root-cause diagnosis difficult. This is a real workflow runtime failure affecting users of vLLM and similar proxies with thinking-capable models.

source_issues.title: Improve Documentation: OpenAI compatible API
source_issues.evidence: User reports that without showThinking:false in judge config, promptfoo tries to parse thinking content as JSON leading to 'Could not parse Json' errors. Debugging was hard because promptfoo doesn't show the string it was trying to parse. Official OpenAI API doesn't expose this issue since it doesn't output thinking tokens.

signals.topic: Docker images unavailable after new releases, breaking automated CI/CD pipelines

ghcr.io image missing for latest release
docker.yml workflow not triggering on tags

eval results UI 500 error large payloads

signals.topic: UI and SQLite eval history expose API keys, Bearer tokens, and OAuth credentials in plain text

API key plaintext in eval database
sensitive headers displayed in promptfoo UI

Users who share debug output (common workflow) will inadvertently leak credentials. Anyone with machine access retrieves all credentials ever used. source_issues.title: UI and stored eval record expose rendered Authorization / apiKey in plain text
source_issues.evidence: UI Details panel and SQLite database store provider config with rendered Authorization headers, API keys, and OAuth tokens in plain text. Sharing a Details blob for debugging purposes leaks live credentials. Reproducible as of 2026-04-20.

signals.topic: OpenRouterProvider silently ignores user-supplied apiBaseUrl, routing traffic to wrong endpoint
signals.summary: OpenRouterProvider hardcodes apiBaseUrl after spreading user config, so any user-supplied apiBaseUrl in promptfooconfig.yaml is silently discarded. Traffic goes to openrouter.ai even when a proxy or compliance gateway is configured.
aliases: openrouter hardcoded base url overrides user config
signals.review_reason: A legitimate and common use case (routing OpenRouter through a compliance gateway or caching proxy) is silently broken. The user's config is accepted without error but completely ignored. Traffic is routed to the wrong endpoint, causing 401s that are hard to trace back to this config override. This is a silent data-routing failure, not just a minor UX issue.

source_issues.title: openrouter provider: hardcoded apiBaseUrl silently overrides user config
source_issues.evidence: Source code confirmed: apiBaseUrl is hardcoded after user config spread, making any user-supplied value silently ignored. User expecting traffic through a compliance gateway or caching proxy gets routed to openrouter.ai instead, typically surfacing as unexpected 401 errors.

signals.topic: Node.hash MetadataMode.ALL 导致静默的全量重新向量化，造成显著算力成本浪费

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Node.hash uses MetadataMode.ALL, causing unnecessary re-embeds when volatile file-stat metadata changes

signals.topic: QueryFusionRetriever 在 reciprocal_rerank 模式下静默忽略 retriever_weights，导致融合结果权重失效

signals.topic: Windows: daemon process silently dies on start and reports incorrect status due to ps -o incompatibility
signals.summary: On Windows (Git Bash/msys2), both `ruflo daemon start` and `ruflo daemon status` fail because the code uses Unix-style `ps -o pid` syntax that is unsupported on Windows. The `start` command reports success but the process exits within ~2s. The `status` command always shows STOPPED even when the daemon is running. Confirmed on both v3.5.7 and v3.5.80, affecting all Windows users.
aliases: ruflo daemon start silent death on Windows
daemon status reports STOPPED on Windows
signals.review_reason: High-frequency Windows-specific blocking issue affecting both daemon start and status commands. The daemon process silently dies after reporting success, making the entire daemon feature unusable on Windows. This is a main-flow failure affecting all Windows users (the most common Windows development environment uses Git Bash). Two independent reports confirm the issue on different versions.

source_issues.title: daemon start silently dies on Windows due to ps -o incompatibility
source_issues.evidence: ruflo daemon start reports '[OK] Daemon started in background (PID: N)' but process exits within ~2s. PID file orphaned, daemon.log stays 0 bytes. Affects both v3.5.7 and v3.5.80 on Windows 11 Git Bash.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Daemon status shows STOPPED on Windows — ps -o pid command not supported
source_issues.evidence: ruflo daemon status always shows 'Status: STOPPED' immediately after starting, even when the daemon process is confirmed running. Root cause: `ps -o pid` syntax not supported on Windows Git Bash/msys2.

signals.topic: ruflo wrapper one-shot commands hang ~2 minutes before exit; AgentDB Patch warnings leak on every invocation
signals.summary: The ruflo wrapper's `bin/ruflo.js` is missing a `.then(() => process.exit(0))` branch on `cli.run()`, causing all one-shot commands (status, --version, etc.) to hang for ~120 seconds before the process exits. Additionally, AgentDB Patch console warnings leak on every invocation because the wrapper bypasses the canonical CLI's console.warn shim, printing spurious messages even for `ruflo --version`.
aliases: ruflo wrapper hangs 2 minutes on exit
AgentDB Patch warning leaks on every ruflo command
signals.review_reason: Blocking UX issue: every one-shot command hangs for 2 minutes after completing work, making the CLI impractical to use interactively. The AgentDB Patch warning spam pollutes all output, degrading signal quality. Both issues are confirmed with full reproduction steps and a PR fix is already available, indicating high confidence. Count=1 because the second bug (AgentDB warning) is part of the same issue.

source_issues.title: ruflo wrapper: one-shot commands hang ~2min + AgentDB Patch warnings leak
source_issues.evidence: Every one-shot command (ruflo status, ruflo --version) hangs for ~120s after producing correct output. AgentDB Patch warning leaks on every invocation including --version. Verified on ruflo@3.5.80, Windows 11, Node 24.14.1. PR #1640 exists with the fix.

signals.topic: MCP worker dispatch, workflow_run, and CLI process workers list all report fabricated/untrustworthy state independent of real daemon execution
signals.summary: Three surfaces advertise worker functionality but do not reflect real daemon execution: (1) `mcp__ruflo__hooks_worker-dispatch` returns 'completed' synchronously without invoking daemon workers and does not increment runCount; (2) `mcp__ruflo__workflow_run` returns agentsSpawned=0 for both dryRun and live invocations using the research template; (3) `ruflo process workers --action list` returns hardcoded demo IDs instead of the real daemon worker registry. Meanwhile, `ruflo daemon trigger --worker <name>` correctly executes work and increments runCount.
aliases: MCP worker dispatch returns fabricated completion without daemon execution
workflow_run reports zero agentsSpawned even in live mode
process workers list returns hardcoded demo IDs not matching daemon registry
signals.review_reason: Three separate surfaces all report fabricated execution state, creating a fundamental trust problem. Users and automation scripts cannot rely on any of these surfaces to determine whether workers actually ran. This is a critical reporting-vs-execution mismatch that affects automated workflows and monitoring.

source_issues.title: MCP hooks_worker-dispatch returns fabricated completion independent of daemon; process workers --action list returns hardcoded demo IDs — same reporting-vs-execution surface-family defect
source_issues.evidence: Verified with reproduction steps: mcp__ruflo__hooks_worker-dispatch returns status:completed in <1s with no runCount increment; ruflo daemon trigger --worker audit correctly increments runCount and returns real output. Three distinct surfaces (MCP dispatch, workflow_run, process workers list) all lie about execution state.

signals.topic: ruflo hooks post-task hangs indefinitely after completing outcome recording until externally killed
signals.summary: `ruflo hooks post-task` records the task outcome successfully (~1.1s) but the Node process never exits on its own, hanging indefinitely. This blocks slash commands in Claude Code and CI scripts that call it synchronously. The hang occurs regardless of stdin payload (empty string, valid JSON, EOF, etc.), indicating a post-completion shutdown bug where an unref'd timer, watcher, or IPC socket keeps the event loop alive.
aliases: ruflo hooks post-task hangs after recording
post-task blocks slash commands and CI scripts
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow runtime blocking issue that causes slash commands and CI scripts to hang indefinitely. The command completes its actual work (recording the outcome) but never exits, making it unusable in any automated context without a timeout wrapper. Count=1 as a single issue, but the impact on CI/CD and slash command workflows is significant.

source_issues.title: ruflo hooks post-task hangs indefinitely after recording outcome (v3.5.80)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed on ruflo@3.5.80, Node v20.19.6, WSL2. All stdin variations tested (empty string, valid JSON, EOF, pipe) cause the same indefinite hang. Process must be killed externally. A /pdx-* slash command hung at 4m 53s before user intervention. Workaround: wrap with `timeout 10`.

signals.topic: ruflo session save crashes with undefined property error and corrupts session list with invalid date rows
signals.summary: `ruflo session save <name>` fails with 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading agentCount)' after printing a misleading 'Session saved' line. This writes a partial record to disk, causing `ruflo session list` to display rows with empty ID, empty name, and 'Invalid Date' timestamps. `ruflo session current` immediately reports 'No active session' after a save that appeared to succeed.
aliases: session save crashes on agentCount undefined
session list shows corrupt Invalid Date rows
session current shows no active session after save
signals.review_reason: Session persistence is a core feature; the crash and subsequent data corruption makes it completely unreliable. Users cannot save sessions across Claude Code runs. Corrupted entries accumulate and cannot be cleaned up since they have no valid ID to target the delete command. This is a main-flow failure for session management.

source_issues.title: ruflo/claude-flow session save crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading agentCount)'; session list shows corrupt Invalid Date rows
source_issues.evidence: Crash confirmed on ruflo v3.5.80, Node v20.19.6, WSL2. Error: TypeError on .agentCount access. Partial record written causes corrupted session list entries that cannot be targeted with session delete (no valid ID). Reproduced without pre-initializing a swarm.

signals.topic: `--args` CLI 参数解析器错误分割含逗号值的 Chrome feature flag，导致 HTTPS 降级等关键行为无法配置
signals.summary: `--args` 参数解析器按每个逗号分割输入，但 Chrome feature flag（如 `--disable-features=...`）的值本身是逗号分隔列表，导致单一 flag 被错误拆分为多个无效参数。用户在本地开发环境中无法禁用 HTTPS-first/HTTPS-upgrade 行为，auth flow 失败。
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1，但影响是主流程阻断：Chrome HTTPS 行为无法在 agent-browser 下配置，导致 auth flow 失败。issue 提供了完整根因分析、复现步骤和已验证的 patch，用户影响明确（auth 失败），非边缘 case。

source_issues.title: `--args` incorrectly splits single Chrome flags whose values contain commas
source_issues.evidence: 作者提供了完整复现步骤和已验证的 patch。使用 stock binary 时，auth URL 无法正常导航（返回 ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT 或挂起）；直接用 Chrome 原生命令传递完整 flag 则成功。根本原因是 cli/src/main.rs 按每个逗号分割 --args，错误地把单个 Chrome 参数拆成多个。

signals.topic: Vertex AI gemini-3 function tool calls fail due to rejected includeServerSideToolInvocations field

signals.topic: useChat resumeStream causes duplicate text and reasoning UI parts — user-visible flickering on network blips

signals.review_reason: Duplicate content visible to end users on resume scenarios (network blips, lifecycle aborts, proxy timeouts) — a noticeable degradation of the streaming UI experience. The bug is confirmed with failing tests, reproduced on latest main branch. While not a complete block, this is a real user-visible issue in common failure/retry scenarios.

source_issues.title: useChat resume duplicates `text` and `reasoning` parts when replaying UIMessage stream

signals.topic: Turbopack blocks Pages Router global CSS when next/font is imported — build fails with misleading error

Workaround (--webpack) exists but defeats the purpose of Turbopack being the default bundler in Next.js 16.

signals.topic: Non-ASCII dynamic route params crash App Router with ERR_INVALID_CHAR on x-next-cache-tags header — ISR completely broken for i18n routes
signals.summary: Any App Router dynamic route with non-ASCII characters (Hebrew, Arabic, Chinese, emoji) in params causes 500 Internal Server Error on every request. Root cause: Next.js writes the matched route path to x-next-cache-tags HTTP header without encoding, violating RFC 7230 (headers must be ASCII). ISR is completely broken for affected routes.
aliases: Hebrew Arabic Chinese emoji route params crash
signals.review_reason: 2 issues reporting the same crash. Main flow is completely blocked: affected App Router routes with non-ASCII params return 500 on every request. ISR is broken. Production-impacting (confirmed on Vercel deployment). No client-side workaround exists. Root cause is clearly identified (unencoded non-ASCII in HTTP header). count=2 with strong evidence.

source_issues.title: App Router: non-ASCII dynamic route params crash with ERR_INVALID_CHAR on x-next-cache-tags header
source_issues.evidence: Open issue with full reproduction repo. curl test shows /hello → 200 OK, /מידע → 500. Root cause identified: x-next-cache-tags header receives raw non-ASCII path without percent-encoding. Only workaround: 'export const dynamic = force-dynamic' which disables ISR entirely. Reproduces on both local next start and Vercel production. Confirmed broken on 16.2.2 and 16.2.4.

source_issues.title: App Router: non-ASCII dynamic route params crash with ERR_INVALID_CHAR on x-next-cache-tags header
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate closed as 'invalid link' (extra line in reproduction section tripped bot). Body is otherwise identical to #93142 with the same detailed evidence.

signals.topic: Metadata descriptions containing Windows carriage returns result in duplicate meta description tags after hydration
signals.summary: When metadata descriptions contain Windows carriage returns (\r\n), Next.js strips them from the SSR HTML but keeps them in the client hydration data, causing a second meta description tag to be inserted during hydration. This creates duplicate meta description tags which harms SEO.
signals.review_reason: SEO-impacting bug: Windows carriage returns in metadata descriptions cause duplicate meta description tags after hydration, which is harmful for SEO. count=2, both reporting the same root cause. Not blocking but has clear user-visible impact (duplicate tags detected by SEO crawlers). P2 due to low severity and availability of simple workaround.

source_issues.title: Metadata descriptions containing Windows carriage returns result in duplicate <meta> tags
source_issues.evidence: Open issue with reproduction repo. document.querySelectorAll('meta[name=description]').length returns 2 instead of 1 after hydration. Windows CR gets stripped in built HTML but not in hydration data, causing Next to re-add the description. Workaround: strip CR with replace(/\r/g, ''). Affects deployed environments.

source_issues.title: Metadata descriptions containing Windows carriage returns result in duplicate <meta> tags
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate closed as 'invalid link' (incomplete reproduction link in issue template). Body contains the same bug report with consistent evidence.

signals.summary: In next dev mode, editing a local image file without changing its filename does not update the image rendered by next/image. The plain img tag shows the updated image but next/image continues showing the old version until .next is deleted and the dev server is restarted.
aliases: image component dev cache not invalidated
local image update not reflected next/image
signals.review_reason: Dev experience regression: next/image in dev shows stale local images after editing without renaming the file. Dev DX issue with count=2 (two reports), linked reproduction, and clear workaround. P2 because it is dev-only and has a simple workaround (rename file or delete .next).

source_issues.evidence: Open issue with reproduction repo. After editing local image file without renaming, plain img shows updated image but next/image shows stale version. signals.topic: Memory leak in Next.js 16.x stable: production services hit OOM crashes — fix stuck in canary 45+ days without stable backport
signals.summary: A confirmed memory leak (arrayBuffers not released, WriteWrap._chunks retainer chain) causes production Next.js 16.x stable services to accumulate memory until OOM. Fix exists in canary (PRs #88577, #89040) but has not been released in any 16.x stable for 45+ days. Real production services are experiencing repeated OOM kills.
aliases: fetch response tee memory growth production
production OOM not fixed in stable release
signals.review_reason: Despite count=1, this meets P0 criteria due to overwhelming user impact evidence: documented production OOM kills (4 in 7 days), service climbing ~30 MiB/hour at idle, clear regression from prior releases, fix exists but withheld from stable for 45+ days. The exclusion rule for count<3 applies only when review_reason lacks strong evidence — this issue has extremely strong evidence of production service failures.

source_issues.title: Memory leak fix from canary (PRs #88577, #89040) still not in any 16.x stable release 45+ days later — production OOMs ongoing on 16.2.4
source_issues.evidence: Documented production impact: service on Render (512 MiB cap) climbs ~30 MiB/hour at idle, hits OOM cap in ~8 hours, gets killed. 4 confirmed OOM kills in 7 days. Reproduces across all 16.x stable versions (16.0.x through 16.2.4). Canary 16.3.0-canary.2 confirmed to NOT leak. Bug matches the tee'd stream fingerprint from #90898 exactly. Multiple prior issues filed, each closed as 'completed' (fix in canary only) with no stable backport. Only workaround: run canary in production.

signals.topic: SDK `getProjects` API 返回响应验证失败（Zod schema 与实际 API 响应不匹配）
signals.summary: 用户调用 `getProjects` 接口后，SDK 的 Zod schema 无法正确解析 API 返回的响应，导致抛出大量 ZodError 验证错误，阻断主流程。问题在 SDK 从 1.18.7 升级到 1.18.9 后出现，涉及 `alias` 字段类型不匹配（期望 array 但收到 undefined）及 `security` 字段联合类型解析失败。
signals.review_reason: 这是典型的 SDK 主流程阻断问题：`getProjects` 是高频核心 API，schema 与实际响应不匹配直接导致所有调用者无法正常使用，升级引入回归属主流程阻断。虽仅单条 issue，但错误规模极大（46 个项目验证失败），有 5 条评论活跃讨论，清楚表明真实用户影响。

source_issues.title: `getProjects` response validation error
source_issues.evidence: 用户在升级 SDK 1.18.7 → 1.18.9 后，`getProjects` 调用直接抛出 ZodError，错误涉及 projects 数组中 46 个项目的 alias 字段（期望 array 收到 undefined）及 security 字段联合类型解析失败。主流程完全阻断，5 条评论持续活跃讨论。

signals.topic: Turborepo incorrectly resolves peer dependencies as workspace dependencies when concrete npm dep exists
signals.summary: When a package has a peer dependency pointing to a workspace package and a concrete npm dependency of the same name, Turbo incorrectly includes the workspace as a dependency in its build graph, causing extra tasks to run unnecessarily. This deviates from Yarn's expected behavior.
aliases: peer deps incorrectly treated as workspace deps
workspace dependency graph incorrect with peer deps
signals.review_reason: Two issues sharing the same root cause: Turbo's dependency graph resolver incorrectly pulls in workspace packages when the user has a concrete npm-sourced dependency of the same name. This is not a blocking failure but causes incorrect task scheduling (extra builds, wasted CI time, wrong topological order). For Yarn 4 users with `enableTransparentWorkspaces: false`, this can cause FFI packages to be built locally when they should use the npm version, which is potentially a CI/build failure in FFI contexts.

source_issues.title: Turborepo incorrectly viewing as peer deps as workspace dependencies when concrete npm dependency exists
source_issues.evidence: When a concrete npm devDependency and a peer dep pointing to a workspace package of the same name coexist, Turbo builds the workspace as a dependency when it should not. Extra tasks run (buffer, d, e) that should not run.

source_issues.title: Yarn 4: Respect `enableTransparentWorkspaces: false` when resolving workspace dependencies
source_issues.evidence: When a dependency uses Yarn's npm: protocol with the same name as a workspace, Turbo incorrectly builds the workspace even though the dependency comes from npm. Reproduction repo shows buffer workspace's build script is incorrectly run despite not being a dependency.

signals.topic: pnpm 11 multi-document YAML lockfile causes workspace resolution failure and task breakdown
signals.summary: Turbo's lockfile parser cannot handle pnpm 11's multi-document YAML lockfile format (which includes `pnpmfileChecksum` frontmatter when `configDependencies` or `packageExtensions` are used). This causes workspace resolution to fail and tasks to break when pnpmfile hooks are registered.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary workflow blocker. When pnpm 11 generates a multi-document YAML lockfile (required for `configDependencies`), Turbo fails to resolve workspaces, which cascades into task-level failures. The user demonstrates that `pnpm -r run typecheck` (without turbo) works correctly — the failure is exclusively introduced by Turbo. Both the warning and the hard failure are reproducible.

source_issues.title: Turbo cannot parse pnpm 11 lockfiles with multi-document YAML (configDependencies)
source_issues.evidence: Turbo emits warning 'Unable to convert to yaml: deserializing from YAML containing more than one document is not supported', workspace resolution fails, tasks break with 'Error during pnpmfile execution: Cannot find module'

signals.topic: Turborepo cache miss after deleting output files from .turbo/cache/
signals.summary: After a successful cached build, if a user deletes the output files from the local project directory (e.g., `apps/nuxt/.output`), a subsequent `turbo build` returns a cache miss and triggers a full rebuild instead of restoring the deleted outputs from the `.turbo/cache/` archive.
aliases: cache artifact mismatch after output deletion
turbo build cache miss from output files removed
signals.review_reason: Cache miss after output deletion defeats Turbo's core value proposition — incremental builds. The user clearly demonstrates that after a FULL TURBO cache hit, deleting the output directory causes the next build to miss the cache and rebuild instead of restoring from the existing `.turbo/cache/xxx.tar.zst`. This is a direct failure of cache artifact integrity detection and constitutes a significant workflow regression.

source_issues.title: Cache miss after deleting output files
source_issues.evidence: Steps: build (cache hit), delete apps/nuxt/.output, build again → cache miss instead of cache restore. Reproduction repo provided at gyhyfj/tuborepo-cache-miss.

signals.topic: Turborepo AI skill dispatcher incorrectly rejects valid root task configurations
signals.summary: The shipped Turborepo AI skill's command dispatcher contains an absolute rule ('DO NOT create Root Tasks') that contradicts the skill's own SKILL.md guidance and Turborepo's official documentation. This causes AI agents using the skill to reject valid root task configurations like Vitest Projects' `//#test`.
aliases: skill command dispatcher root task guidance incorrect
AI agent generates incorrect turbo.json for root tasks
signals.review_reason: While this is an AI tooling guidance issue rather than a core runtime failure, it constitutes a real user pain point for developers using the Turborepo skill with AI coding agents. Agents following the dispatcher produce incorrect turbo.json configurations, forcing users to manually override the AI-generated output. The impact is UX friction and misconfiguration rather than build failures, making it P2.

source_issues.title: Turborepo skill: command dispatcher contradicts SKILL.md on Root Tasks
source_issues.evidence: The command/turborepo.md dispatcher rule 'DO NOT create Root Tasks' contradicts SKILL.md which says root tasks are valid 'only for tasks that truly cannot exist in packages (rare)'. Agents following the dispatcher reject Vitest Projects' //#test and other valid root task use cases. Downstream PR that triggered this: ValescoAgency/millsreg-sanity#67.

signals.topic: Vercel Toolbar iframe blocked by COEP due to missing CORP header on vercel.live
signals.summary: When user apps set Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy (COEP) headers, the Vercel Toolbar iframe loaded from vercel.live is blocked because the response lacks Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy (CORP) headers. This breaks the postMessage handshake, preventing the toolbar from rendering on preview deployments.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point. The Vercel Toolbar is a key developer experience feature that becomes completely non-functional when customers follow Chrome's Spectre mitigation guidance (COEP credentialless). The issue has clear reproduction steps, visible browser errors, and forces users to reduce their security posture as a workaround. It blocks a specific but growing user segment (COEP-strict apps).

source_issues.title: @vercel/toolbar iframe from vercel.live missing CORP header, fails to embed under COEP=credentialless
source_issues.evidence: Customers with COEP-strict apps (COEP=credentialless or require-corp) cannot use the Vercel Toolbar on preview deployments. Browser console shows: 'Unsafe attempt to load URL https://vercel.live/_next-live/feedback/feedback.html... from frame with URL chrome-error://chromewebdata/'. Workaround requires dropping COEP to 'unsafe-none' on preview environments, reducing app isolation guarantees.

signals.topic: Next.js 16 post-build validation ENOENT failures on multi-segment Root Directory
signals.summary: When a project uses a multi-segment Root Directory (e.g., clients/admin-ui), Next.js 16's post-build validation computes expected file paths using only the basename, dropping intermediate path segments. This causes ENOENT errors on files that exist at the correct location, blocking deployments entirely.
aliases: Root Directory path truncation in validation
signals.review_reason: This is a deployment-blocking bug. The post-build validation step fails after a successful build, preventing the deployment from completing. For monorepo users with multi-segment Root Directory paths (a common pattern in npm workspaces setups), this completely blocks the primary workflow (deployment). The workaround of creating symlinks is non-obvious and requires custom build logic.

source_issues.title: Next.js 16 post-build validation drops intermediate path segments from multi-segment Root Directory
source_issues.evidence: Deployments fail with ENOENT errors for files that exist on disk at correct paths. The validator uses '/vercel/path0/admin-ui/' instead of '/vercel/path0/clients/admin-ui/', dropping the 'clients/' prefix. The build itself completes successfully but post-build validation runs after output is written and causes the deployment to fail. Workaround requires creating symlinks during build, which is a manual and fragile fix.

signals.topic: CLI `vc link` links wrong project and deploys to incorrect target
signals.summary: When running `vc link` with an explicit project ID or name, the CLI correctly writes the project name and ID to .vercel/project.json but uses the wrong OIDC token scoped to a different project. This causes all subsequent deployments to go to the wrong project, silently misrouting code changes.
aliases: CLI linking selects incorrect project scope
signals.review_reason: This is a critical deployment misrouting bug. The core CLI linking workflow appears to succeed but silently attaches the wrong project credentials. Subsequent deployments go to the wrong target, meaning code changes are deployed to the wrong project without the user's knowledge. This directly breaks the primary developer workflow (link → deploy) and could cause production incidents if users don't notice the wrong URL. The bug is reproducible and has visible evidence of wrong project deployment.

source_issues.title: CLI: I can't deploy because `vc link` keeps linking wrong project
source_issues.evidence: User runs 'vc link --project prj_QBlGvMRXwA2TkPHGcjeUWuukjMmh' targeting 'covillage-portal'. The CLI confirms linking to 'covillage-portal' and writes project.json correctly, but downloads env vars from 'covillage' and writes the wrong VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN. Every subsequent deploy goes to 'covillage' instead of 'covillage-portal'. The user confirmed via dashboard screenshot that deployments land on the wrong project.

signals.topic: CLI `vercel redeploy` fails with authorization error due to inconsistent env var handling vs other commands
signals.summary: Commands like `vercel list` correctly honor VERCEL_ORG_ID / VERCEL_PROJECT_ID environment variables, but `vercel redeploy` bypasses getLinkedProject and calls getScope directly, resolving the default team instead of the token-scoped team. This causes 'Not authorized' errors when the token is scoped to a different team than the user's default.
aliases: vercel redeploy auth failure org id
getScope does not honor token-scoped team
signals.review_reason: This is an auth/authorization bug affecting CLI redeploy in CI/CD environments. When users set VERCEL_ORG_ID and a token scoped to a specific team (a standard CI pattern), other commands work but redeploy fails with a clear authorization error, blocking the redeploy workflow. The inconsistency between commands is a UX and correctness issue that breaks expected behavior for users following standard CI configuration patterns.

source_issues.title: Inconsistent cli flow between `list` and `redeploy` with env vars `VERCEL_ORG_ID`
source_issues.evidence: In CI environments using VERCEL_ORG_ID and VERCEL_TOKEN (scoped to a specific team), 'vercel list' works correctly but 'vercel redeploy' fails with 'Not authorized: Trying to access resource under scope <team>. You must re-authenticate to this scope or use a token with access to this scope.' Root cause: redeploy does not call getLinkedProject, instead uses getScope which resolves the default team, not the token-scoped team.

signals.topic: Extension install fails with 'Invalid gzip header' on Windows/macOS — key extensions unavailable
signals.summary: Zed fails to install any extensions on Windows 11 25H2 and macOS. The extension archive download is corrupted mid-transfer (response truncated/rewritten), causing gzip decompression to fail with 'Invalid gzip header', leaving extensions uninstalled with no user-actionable error in the UI.
signals.review_reason: Extension installation is a core feature of Zed's extensibility model. Both Windows and macOS users are completely blocked from installing or updating extensions — a critical regression for power users relying on language-specific extensions, themes, or language servers delivered via extensions.

source_issues.title: Unable to install extensions on Windows 11 25H2 (Invalid gzip header)
source_issues.evidence: Windows 11 25H2: multiple extensions (csv, vue, opencode) all fail with 'Invalid gzip header'. Log shows: 'failed to iterate over archive / Caused by: Invalid gzip header / No extension manifest found'. Zed log confirms extension install loop fails consistently.

source_issues.title: Unable to install extensions.
source_issues.evidence: macOS 26.3.1: Server returns 'InvalidAccessKeyId' for extension archive download, then 'Invalid gzip header' in local log. Multiple existing extensions fail to load (catppuccin, toml, html, macos-classic, material-icon-theme, git-firefly). Extension ecosystem completely broken.

signals.topic: Agent Panel ACP: streaming responses get mixed across threads when switching mid-generation
signals.summary: When using the Agent Panel with Factory Droid ACP, opening a new thread causes the old session's streaming text to appear in the new thread, or switching threads mid-generation causes responses intended for one thread to be appended to another thread's transcript. Session isolation is broken.
signals.review_reason: Agent Panel is a primary AI-powered workflow feature. Thread response mixing is a data-integrity issue that corrupts conversation history and breaks multi-task workflows. Users relying on parallel agent threads for different tasks are blocked from safe concurrent usage.

source_issues.title: Droid ACP does not allow for parallel sessions
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction: open Droid ACP, send a longer prompt, open a new thread — the old session's streaming text appears in the new thread's view. Evidence: screenshot shared showing cross-thread text contamination. Verified on Zed Nightly v0.235.0.

source_issues.title: Streamed response from one thread is appended to another thread when switching threads mid-generation (Factory Droid via ACP)
source_issues.evidence: User traces the dispatch path in Zed source code and concludes the bug likely lives in the Factory Droid CLI emitting session/update notifications with wrong sessionId. Reproduction: generate response in Thread B, switch to Thread A mid-stream — Thread B's response renders inside Thread A transcript. Workaround: avoid switching threads until generation completes.

signals.topic: Application crashes on Windows, fails to load database file, becomes unusable after restart
signals.summary: Zed crashes during a session and then becomes completely unusable on restart. The app throttles CPU but never opens, with the root cause being a database file load failure. No recovery path exists for the user — the app must be force-closed and cannot be reopened.
signals.review_reason: Application becomes completely unusable after a crash — no recovery path. This is a full application blockage: the editor cannot be started at all after the initial crash, making it a P0 for affected users. Count=1 but evidence of total startup failure with no user-visible recovery guidance justifies P0.

source_issues.title: The application crashed
source_issues.evidence: Windows 11 25H2: app crashed and wouldn't open any more files. After force-closing, app still throttles processor on restart but never opens. Error: 'Failed to load the database file.' No settings, extensions, or plugins installed — default configuration. 2 comments from other users likely affected.

signals.topic: Metal atlas memory leak on macOS causes application panic after extended sessions
signals.summary: After ~67 hours of a Zed session with many image/emoji renders, the Metal atlas becomes fragmented due to two memory leaks: MetalAtlas::remove never deallocates from the etagere allocator, and glyph tiles are never evicted from tiles_by_key. This leads to allocation failures, then a nil-texture panic at MetalAtlasTexture::bytes_per_pixel with 'not implemented'. Zed crashes and restarts, losing all unsaved work.
signals.review_reason: Application panic causes data loss for all open workspaces. The leak is systematic: every extended session will eventually crash. Two independent memory leaks in the Metal atlas tile management are identified with full technical analysis. Sentry minidump confirms the crash. P0 due to complete application crash with potential data loss.

source_issues.title: MetalAtlas::bytes_per_pixel 'not implemented' on macOS after long session with many images
source_issues.evidence: Full root-cause analysis provided: 9,421 'failed to allocate' log entries accumulate over ~67 hours. Metal atlas allocator leaks in two places (no deallocate call in remove, no glyph tile eviction). Panic fires at metal_atlas.rs:244 with 'not implemented'. Minidump already uploaded to Sentry. Only occurs after extended sessions with many images/emoji — not a simple repro but impact is total session loss on crash.

signals.topic: Settings UI on Windows silently fails to write settings when file is read-only or locked
signals.summary: On Windows, when the settings file is read-only (or locked), Zed's Settings UI silently fails to persist changes. There is no toast, banner, or error message — the user changes a setting (theme, font, etc.) but it silently reverts. The TODO comment 'todo(settings_ui) don't log err' in the codebase acknowledges this was known to be incomplete.
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss: users believe their settings are saved but they are not. Particularly dangerous on Windows where file permission errors are common. The app acknowledges internally via TODO that this is known-incomplete behavior. No user-facing recovery path when settings fail to write.

source_issues.title: Static icon theme from Dynamic + System mode always uses the dark slot (mislabeled — actual issue: settings write silently fails)
source_issues.evidence: Windows 11: set settings.json to read-only, change a setting via Settings UI — no visible error. Toast/banner absent. Failure logged internally only. TODO comment in code: 'todo(settings_ui) don't log err'. User receives zero feedback that their change was not saved. Affects all Settings UI controls that call update_settings_file.
